# State source audit — all catalogued routes

Research cutoff: **2026-08-25**. Scope is every route in `data/state-sources.js` (50 states), checked against the official agency, comptroller, auditor, treasurer, legislature, or state open-data page/API/PDF. Counts and totals below are source measures already validated in the repository's state modules or source notes; they are not combined across portals, fiscal bases, or periods. `FY2024` follows each source's own fiscal-year convention. Deferred, access-blocked, wrong-period, and corrupted routes are retained in the structured [source failure ledger](data/source-failures.json) and are not promoted into pie data.

## Interpretation rules

- A validated total means the official file/API/page's own rows or summaries reconcile within the stated precision. It does not mean statewide coverage, GAAP equivalence, or comparability with another state's measure.
- ACFR activity rows, budget actuals, agency summaries, vendor aggregates, purchase orders, and cash/checkbook payments remain separate measures even when they cover the same fiscal year.
- “Partial” is intentional: official exclusions, participating-agency limits, branch limits, missing entities, redaction, unaudited status, or a different accounting basis prevent a statewide denominator claim.
- Summary files do not insert a synthetic `Others` or residual row. Each pie uses one official itemized source layer, records its exact `itemizedTotal`, and keeps the separate Census/CBO comparator in `comparison` metadata with a source link. A comparator difference is not assigned to a receiver or program without official source rows.
- The Census FY2024 mutually exclusive function/category layer remains the comparable cross-state control in each state summary. The allocation panel now defaults to the restored, state-specific official source layer instead, and presents Census only as a separately selected function view; the two are never merged. The federal pie uses the precise Treasury MTS budget-function layer, with USAspending agency/account data retained as a non-additive drill-down.
- Singular `Other` labels remain only when they are the official source's fund, account, object-class, agency, or program name; they are not invented residual buckets. Any source that cannot expose a finer validated crosswalk remains linked and documented as scope-limited.
- `test-department-data.js` maintains the explicit allowlist for the 22 source-defined `Other` labels; an unlisted label or an unitemized label fails validation.
- Itemized amounts are no longer scaled to a Census/CBO comparator. The displayed `amount` and `sourceAmount` use the official source basis; the separate comparator and its difference remain visible as metadata so incompatible accounting scopes are not silently combined.
- Negative accounting adjustments remain in the itemized data. The pie geometry uses positive outlay amounts and normalizes those positive slices to 100%; negative rows remain clickable/listed as adjustments instead of being drawn as negative wedges.
- Cross-checks treat sub-dollar disagreements as agreements when the underlying sources use different rounding, while exact-cent reconciliations are retained where available.
- Skipped or failed routes are retained as official leads with the failure mode recorded; they are not promoted into JavaScript data modules until a period-aligned, reproducible total is available.

# Federal source research

Research date: 2026-08-18. Scope: official primary sources only. No spending amounts are copied here; this is a source and importability ledger.

## Import rules

- Keep `measure` explicit: `outlay`, `obligation`, `budgetary_resource`, `disbursement`, `refund`, `cost`, or `payment` are not interchangeable.
- Keep `basis` explicit: modified cash, award/account reporting, GAAP net cost, program reimbursement, or survey/reporting data.
- A row is safe for the national outlay pie only when it is a mutually exclusive slice of the same fiscal-year measure and reconciles to a primary denominator. Agency/program/drug/recipient rows are drill-downs unless the source explicitly defines them as the denominator.
- Federal transfers and federal program payments can appear again in state or grantee datasets. Never add those rows to federal totals without an intergovernmental-transfer reconciliation.

## Verified source matrix

| Owner / source | Exact URL or endpoint | FY / vintage and units | Itemized dimensions | Additive or nested? | Safe import decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **U.S. Treasury / Fiscal Service — Monthly Treasury Statement (MTS)** | [FY2024 final MTS PDF](https://fiscal.treasury.gov/system/files/files/reports-statements/mts/mts0924.pdf); [federal-spending guide](https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/americas-finance-guide/federal-spending/) | Final FY2024 through 2024-09-30; tables state `[$ millions]`; modified-cash basis; refunds reduce gross receipts and reimbursements/refunds reduce gross outlays. | Month, receipts by source, outlays by agency, outlays by budget function, on/off-budget, trust funds, and financing. | Tables are mutually exclusive only within their own defined denominator. Agency, function, and program views are alternative rollups; negative offsetting receipts and intra-governmental flows require special handling. | **Safe benchmark import** for the federal-wide cash denominator after PDF extraction and table-level validation. Do not add agency/program rows to function rows. |
| **U.S. Treasury / Fiscal Data — Financial Report of the U.S. Government** | [Verified dataset page and API/download controls](https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/u-s-government-financial-report/statements-of-changes-in-social-insurance-amounts) | FY2024 release; amounts in the dataset's published currency fields, including gross cost in billions for the Statements of Net Cost table; GAAP basis, not cash outlays. | Fiscal year, restatement flag, agency, gross cost, and net-cost statement fields. | Agency rows roll into consolidated financial statements; restatements are alternative vintages, not additional spending. | **Safe as a separate GAAP cost layer only.** Never merge into the MTS/USAspending outlay pie. |
| **Treasury / Fiscal Service — MTS static-report path** | [Published-report path](https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/static-data/published-reports/mts/) | Monthly vintages; report-native units, usually millions of dollars. | Same MTS dimensions as above. | Same MTS rules. | **Conditional.** Use the working `fiscal.treasury.gov` FY2024 URL above when the `fiscaldata` static path is unavailable. |
| **USAspending.gov — government-wide award and account data** | [API root](https://api.usaspending.gov/); [endpoint index](https://api.usaspending.gov/docs/endpoints); [top-tier agencies](https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/references/toptier_agencies/); [spending-by-award](https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_award/); [award download](https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/download/awards/); [transaction download](https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/download/transactions/); [account object classes](https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/federal_accounts/<ACCOUNT_CODE>/available_object_classes/) | Current API/v2; fiscal-year and reporting-period filters; dollar-valued obligations, outlays, budgetary resources, or transaction amounts depending on endpoint. | Awarding/funding agency and subagency, federal account/TAS, program activity, object class, award type, recipient/legal entity, CFDA/Assistance Listing, PSC/NAICS, geography, transaction, subaward, fiscal year/period. | Aggregations are nested and measure-specific. Award obligations are not account outlays; recipient, subaward, program, and agency views can overlap. A grouping can sum only when filters and measure are identical and categories are disjoint. | **Safe primary drill-down backbone** for all agencies, with an explicit measure/basis field. Use account outlays for outlay comparisons; do not present award obligations as cash spent. |
| **CMS — public data API** | [API documentation](https://data.cms.gov/api-docs); endpoint form documented by CMS: `https://data.cms.gov/data-api/v1/dataset/{dataset-id}/data` | Dataset-specific; current annual drug releases include 2020–2024 fields; quarterly datasets are preliminary and carry a current quarter vintage. Currency is dataset-defined spending/reimbursement; dosage units and claims are separate units. | Drug/HCPCS or NDC, brand/generic name, manufacturer, year/quarter, total spending, dosage units, claims, average spending per unit/claim, beneficiary/use fields, outlier flag. | Drug rows are program-level detail, not a federal budget rollup. Medicare Part D uses gross drug cost including Medicare, plan, and beneficiary payments and excludes disclosed manufacturer rebates; Medicaid total reimbursement includes federal and state reimbursement and is not reduced by rebates. | **Safe as a separate CMS program layer** after preserving program, gross/net/rebate, and vintage fields. **Not safe for the federal-total pie** and not additive to MTS or USAspending without payer reconciliation. |
| **CMS — Medicare & Medicaid spending by drug** | [Program landing page](https://data.cms.gov/summary-statistics-on-use-and-payments/medicare-medicaid-spending-by-drug); [Medicare Part D data](https://data.cms.gov/summary-statistics-on-use-and-payments/medicare-medicaid-spending-by-drug/medicare-part-d-spending-by-drug); [Medicaid data dictionary](https://data.cms.gov/resources/medicaid-spending-by-drug-data-dictionary); [Medicaid dashboard/machine-readable file description](https://data.cms.gov/tools/medicaid-drug-spending-dashboard) | Annual Part D latest available 2024 on the verified page; quarterly data is preliminary; Medicaid dictionary includes annual fields through 2024. | Drug, manufacturer, total spending, dosage units, claims, average spending per dosage unit/claim, and outlier indicators. | Nested under CMS program and drug; manufacturer rows must not be summed with drug totals unless the file defines them as disjoint. | **Conditional safe import** for drug/program drill-down. Preserve the official data dictionary and outlier flags. |
| **USDA Farm Service Agency — farm payment files** | [Payment Files Information](https://www.fsa.usda.gov/tools/informational/freedom-information-act-foia/electronic-reading-room/frequently-requested/payment-files) | 2024 and 2025 files are published; Excel flat files; payment amounts are currency fields; page does not label these as the federal fiscal-year outlay ledger. | Recipient name/address, state grouping, payment/program file, and payment amount. | Payments are recipient-level detail within USDA programs. They can overlap USDA agency outlays and USAspending awards and may be organized by program/payment year rather than federal FY. | **Conditional program-layer import.** Keep the file vintage, program/payment-year semantics, and recipient privacy rules. | **USDA Rural Development — Rural Data Gateway** | [Rural Data Gateway](https://www.rd.usda.gov/rural-data-gateway); [FOIA/data description](https://www.rd.usda.gov/contact-us/freedom-information-act-foia) | Public dashboards advertise ten years of downloadable investment data; fiscal-year views; dollars/obligated investment fields, with loans, grants, loan guarantees, and technical assistance distinguished. | Program area, state, county, congressional district, industry sector, investment type/instrument, and fiscal year. | Grant/loan/guarantee/technical-assistance investments are separate instruments; a loan guarantee is not the same as a cash outlay. Geographic and program views are nested. | **Safe as a separate USDA investment layer** only when instrument and `obligated` versus `outlay` are preserved. Not a federal cash-total denominator. |
| **USDOT Federal Transit Administration — National Transit Database (NTD)** | [Funding Sources by Expense Type and Agency](https://data.transportation.gov/Public-Transit/NTD-Annual-Data-View-Funding-Sources-by-Expense-Ty/ujv8-f24s); Socrata resource form: `https://data.transportation.gov/resource/ujv8-f24s.json` | Dataset page describes 2022–2023 report-year data; page updated 2026-07-07; capital and operating expense/funding-source categories. Units are agency-reported financial amounts. | NTD ID, transit agency, mode/source, expense type, capital versus operating, report year, and funding source. | Includes federal, state, local, passenger, and other funding sources; agency view is an aggregation of lower-level mode data. | **Not safe for the federal total.** Safe only as a DOT/NTD operating-and-capital context layer after filtering the federal funding-source field and documenting that it is transit-agency reporting, not Treasury outlays. |
| **HUD — Integrated Disbursement and Information System (IDIS)** | [IDIS data-extract file layouts](https://files.hudexchange.info/resources/documents/IDIS-Online-Appendix-D-Data-Extract-File-Layouts.pdf); [IDIS reports guide](https://files.hudexchange.info/resources/documents/IDIS-Online-Reports-User-Guide.pdf); [CPD public plans/CAPER page](https://cpd.hud.gov/cpd-public/consolidated-plans) | Live/authorized IDIS extracts; public CPD page exposes plan years including 2024; extract files are compressed ASCII, with program financial fields. | Grant, subfund/subgrant, grantee, activity, funding source, CDBG/ESG/HOME/HOPWA financial extracts, draw history, and draw transactions. | Draws/expenditures are nested under grant, funding source, activity, and grantee. The same money can be represented as grant obligation, draw, or expenditure. | **Skipped for direct import pending authorized extract access.** Use USAspending for public HUD award/account data; do not infer IDIS expenditure totals from public plans. |
| **Department of Veterans Affairs — VA Open Data** | [FY2024 veteran pension expenditures by state](https://www.data.va.gov/dataset/Veteran-Pension-Expenditures-By-State-of-Residence/sbtk-kfnm); Socrata resource form: `https://data.va.gov/resource/sbtk-kfnm.json`; [VA budget/finance index](https://department.va.gov/about/va-plans-budget-finances-and-performance/) | Dataset is labeled FY2024; state-level expenditure data; units are dataset-defined expenditure dollars. VA budget/finance index also links agency financial reports and budget documents. | State of residence and pension expenditure dimensions exposed by the dataset; agency financial reports add appropriation/program/budget-resource dimensions. | State pension rows are a VA program subset and nested within VA-wide spending; they are not additive to VA total or federal total. | **Conditional safe import** for the pension drill-down after local schema/HTTP validation. Use VA financial reports as corroboration, not as a second additive total. |
| **Department of Education / Federal Student Aid — annual disbursements** | [Annual disbursements landing page](https://studentaid.gov/data-center/student/annual-disbursements); [FY2024 FSA Annual Report](https://studentaid.gov/sites/default/files/fy2024-fsa-annual-report.pdf); [machine-readable My Aid layout](https://fsapartners.ed.gov/sites/default/files/2023-02/DownloadMyAidDataFileLayout.pdf) | FY2024 annual report; Table 4 reports program aid disbursed in dollars in millions. Student-level My Aid file is user-specific, not a public aggregate. | Direct Loan, Pell, FSEOG, TEACH, IASG, Federal Work-Study, award year, and aid disbursement. | Program rows are nested under FSA and include loans and grants with different budget/outlay treatment. Student-level files are not a public government-wide spending file. | **Safe as an FSA program layer only** from the official annual/data-center reports after extracting the report table. Do not add gross loan disbursement to MTS outlays without loan-accounting reconciliation. Skip student-level files. |

State refund rows are not federal spending beneficiaries in the outlay sense. | **Safe separate import** for refunds and IRS operating-cost drill-downs, with `measure=refund control/geography/program` or `measure=cost control/subtotal/leaf`. Never add refunds to the federal outlay denominator. |
| **Office of Personnel Management — Federal Workforce Data / EHRI** | [FWD home](https://data.opm.gov/); [raw data downloads](https://data.opm.gov/explore-data/data/data-downloads); [getting started and definitions](https://data.opm.gov/info-and-help/getting-started); [EHRI data standards](https://data.opm.gov/data-standards/ehri-data-standards) | Monthly vintage; verified page shows data through June 2026; raw files are TXT/JSON; pay fields are employee/pay-period values, while employment/accessions/separations are counts. | Agency/subelement, employee status, pay plan/grade, occupation, duty station, pay-period payroll fields, employment, accessions, separations, and time. | Employee/pay-period records roll to agency/workforce summaries; payroll data is not the same as agency outlays and may omit employer-side costs or non-civilian personnel. | **Safe as a payroll/workforce context layer only.** Do not use it as a federal payroll total unless the payroll vintage, pay fields, civilian scope, missing records, and reconciliation to Treasury/agency accounts are documented. |

## Cross-checks and reconciliation rules

1. **Federal denominator:** the active pie uses the [final MTS](https://fiscal.treasury.gov/system/files/files/reports-statements/mts/mts0924.pdf) budget-function rows. The 19 checked rows sum to the precise FY2024 outlay total of **$6,751,552,000,000**, including the negative offsetting-receipts row. The prior 75 USAspending agency/object-class detail files remain in `data/federal/archive-agency-source/` as a non-additive receiver/agency layer. The MTS itself warns that details can differ from totals because of rounding and includes negative/offsetting categories.
2. **Agency check:** compare an agency's MTS outlay row with [USAspending's same-FY agency/account outlay view](https://api.usaspending.gov/docs/endpoints) only as a diagnostic. They are different reporting systems and can differ by basis, timing, off-budget treatment, and account coverage; a mismatch is not permission to add both.
3. **Program check:** keep every agency dataset above in a separate `source_layer`. A CMS drug total, USDA payment, HUD draw, VA pension row, FSA disbursement, IRS refund, or OPM payroll row is a drill-down or a different measure unless it explicitly reconciles to the chosen federal denominator.
4. **Refund check:** IRS refunds must be modeled as negative receipts/receipt deductions, matching the MTS treatment, not as positive outlay slices.
5. **Loans and guarantees:** USDA Rural Development and Education loan figures require credit-account treatment; obligations/disbursements are not automatically cash outlays.
6. **No amounts were fabricated or imported from a source whose file could not be validated.**

Each response reconciles exactly to its agency budgetary-resources outlay total, including Agriculture **$233,005,888,496.86** as a checked example. | Replaces the prior unspecified reconciliation row in the 18 affected detail files and adds detail files for 47 formerly summary-only agencies. ## Minimal normalized record for future imports

```text
source_id,owner,program,record_vintage,fiscal_year,period,
measure,basis,amount,unit,receiver,agency,account,program_activity,
object_class,award_id,geography,instrument,parent_source_id,source_url,

```

`parent_source_id` is required for nested drill-downs. `import_status` should be one of `safe`, `conditional`, `skipped`, or `failed`; no row should enter the pie until it has a denominator and a passing reconciliation check.

## CMS FY2024 drug-spending program layers — validated and imported

- **Official catalog:** [CMS data catalog](https://data.cms.gov/data.json) lists **Medicare Part D Spending by Drug : 2024-01-01** with API dataset ID `7e0b4365-fd63-4a29-8f5e-e0ac9f66a81b` and FY2024 temporal coverage.

## USDA/FSA 2024 payment workbook — conditional source, packaged separately

- **Official source:** [FSA Payment Files Information](https://www.fsa.usda.gov/tools/informational/freedom-of-information-act-foia/electronic-reading-room/frequently-requested/payment-files); [workbook landing page](https://www.fsa.usda.gov/documents/state-al-infoianapmt24finaldt25002); [direct XLSX](https://www.fsa.usda.gov/sites/default/files/2025-01/state%20al-in.foia_.na_.pmt24.final_.dt25002.xlsx).

- **Official documentation:** [IDIS Online Data Download Definitions](https://files.hudexchange.info/resources/documents/IDIS-Online-Appendix-D-Data-Extract-File-Layouts.pdf) documents seventeen IDIS extract categories, including CDBG, HOME, ESG, HTF, and HOPWA financial data. - **Access test:** the [public IDIS portal](https://idis.hud.gov/idis/grants.do?submit=View+Grants) requires an authorized username/password and agreement to its terms; no public FY2024 extract URL or downloadable national file was exposed.

  source outlays and endpoint, then proportionally reconciles the displayed

The rows below are **awards or allocations**, not necessarily cash outlays. Each normalized row should carry `benefactor`, `receiver`, `program`, `award_number` (when present), `fiscal_year`, `amount`, `measure`, and `source_url`. None of the sources below contains person-level payroll data in the rows used here; recipients are organizations, public agencies, tribes, transit systems, or state/territory administrative agencies.

Agreement rule: parse visible amount cells, exclude the source's grand-total token, and compare the independent row sum with the published subtotal/total. Differences of **less than $1** are accepted as rounding agreement.

# Federal expansion research: HHS, CDC, NIH, HUD/CPD, and DOL

Research cutoff: **2026-08-19**. Primary official sources only. This note adds federal portals and program layers not represented in `SOURCE_RESEARCH_ALL_SOURCES.md`; it does not edit JavaScript.

## How to read this note

- “FY2024” means federal fiscal year unless the source says **PY2024** or **CY2024**.
- Award, obligation, grant allocation, benefit payment, drawdown, and Treasury outlay are different measures. The amounts below are not additive and must not be inserted into the Treasury outlay denominator without a compatible accounting basis.
- A validated total means the source publishes an official total that matches the described rows or official summary. “Not validated” means the portal was found, but a complete public extract or compatible national total was not available.

## Validated or conditionally validated sources

| Agency / portal | Official download/API and fields | FY2024 measure; count and total | Validation and limitations |
|---|---|---|---|
| **HHS — TAGGS** | [Award Search](https://taggs.hhs.gov/SearchAward?bc=yes); [data dictionary](https://taggs.hhs.gov/About/DataDictionary). The grid and CSV/XLSX exports expose legal entity/recipient, award number, award title, assistance listing, OPDIV, state, issue/funding FY, action date, and award amount. | Full HHS FY2024 total: **not validated**. The unfiltered current grid showed 200,224 award-action items, while exports are limited to 25,000 records. Selected issue-date FY2024 assistance-listing pages provide official subtotals, e.g. [AABD (93.560)](https://taggs.hhs.gov/Detail/CFDADetail?arg_CFDA_NUM=93560) **$21,917,520** and [Policy Research and Evaluation Grants (93.648)](https://taggs.hhs.gov/Detail/CFDADetail?arg_CFDA_NUM=93648) **$13,029,712**. | TAGGS explicitly distinguishes **Issue Date FY** from **Funding FY**. The selected listing subtotals are valid program slices, not a national HHS denominator. TAGGS includes grants, loans, aggregated direct payments, and other assistance; it is an award-action measure, not Treasury cash outlays. |
| **NIH — RePORTER ExPORTER** | [FY2024 project-data download](https://reporter.nih.gov/exporter?index=1&sid=0); [project API data elements](https://api.reporter.nih.gov/documents/Data%20Elements%20for%20RePORTER%20Project%20API_V2.pdf); [NIH Data Book](https://report.nih.gov/nihdatabook/category/1). Bulk project data is a CSV download of roughly **68 MB**, last updated 2025-07-07, with project, organization, fiscal year, institute/center, activity/mechanism, and award/cost fields. | Project row count and summed award amount: **not independently validated here**. Official NIH benchmarks are **$44,945,000,000 FY2024 final budget authority**, **$47,439,000,000 FY2024 operating plan**, and **$37,406,000,000 spending outside NIH**. | The Data Book totals are official NIH budget/funding benchmarks, not a guaranteed row-level reconciliation to ExPORTER. NIH warns that project listings and award amounts may not match year-end categorical-spending reports. ExPORTER includes grants, contracts, intramural projects, and interagency agreements; use it as an NIH itemized award/project layer, not Treasury outlays. |
| **CDC — Public Health Infrastructure Grant (PHIG), Component A** | [FY2024 funding PDF](https://www.cdc.gov/infrastructure-phig/media/pdfs/FY2024-PHIG.pdf); [PHIG overview and FY2024 summary](https://www.cdc.gov/infrastructure-phig/about/index.html). Columns include recipient, Strategy A1 Workforce, A2 Foundational Capabilities, A3 Data Modernization, the immunization-information-system supplement, and FY24 funding grand total. | CDC reports **107 health departments** across states, DC, territories/freely associated states, and large localities. The official FY2024 program page reports approximately **$511 million** awarded to health departments in FY2024. The PDF supplies recipient-level grand-total cells; an exact national sum was **not independently re-summed here**. | This is a CDC grant-obligation/award layer, not CDC total appropriations or Treasury outlays. CDC says PHIG awards are subject to change over the period of performance. The recipient table is suitable for itemized import after downloading the PDF and parsing its grand-total column. |
| **CDC — PHIG, Component B national partners** | [National Partners funding table](https://www.cdc.gov/infrastructure-phig/php/national-partners/index.html). Recipient, FY, and amount are explicit. | **3 FY2024 recipient rows / $185,000,000**: ASTHO $61,923,077; NNPHI $64,384,615; PHAB $58,692,308. The three rows sum exactly to the official FY2024 total. | Five-year PHIG component-B partner awards; not CDC-wide spending and not Treasury outlays. |
| **HUD/CPD — Continuum of Care (CoC) FY2024 competition** | [HUD FY2024 CoC awards](https://www.hud.gov/program_offices/comm_planning/coc/fy_2024_coc_competition); [national award PDF](https://files.hudexchange.info/reports/published/CoC_AwardComp_NatlTerrDC_2024.pdf). HUD provides project/state/CoC Excel and PDF reports with project recipient, CoC, component, project counts, and award amounts. | **6,533 projects / $3,623,037,241** national award. The national report breaks the total into permanent housing, transitional housing, supportive services, HMIS, planning/UFA, new projects, renewals, and YHDP. | The national total is the official competition award total. It is an award/obligation measure, not project drawdowns or Treasury outlays. Project-level information is linked from the HUD Exchange allocations/awards page and should not be added again to the national summary. |
| **HUD/PIH — FY2024 Capital Fund formula awards** | [FY2024 Capital Fund award PDF](https://www.hud.gov/sites/dfiles/PA/documents/FY24-Capital-Fund-Awards.pdf); [HUD executive-director letter](https://www.hud.gov/sites/dfiles/PIH/documents/FY24LettertoExecutiveDirectors.pdf). Rows identify public housing authority and state, with award amount. | **2,756 housing authorities / $3,173,110,086**. The award PDF's Grand Total matches the HUD letter's rounded $3.17 billion announcement. | Related HUD award portal, not CPD. This is a formula-grant award measure for public housing authorities; it is not tenant benefit payment data or Treasury outlays. |
| **DOL/ETA — WIOA PY2024 state allotments** | [Final WIOA Youth table](https://www.dol.gov/node/183816), [Adult table](https://www.dol.gov/node/183817), and [Dislocated Worker table](https://www.dol.gov/node/183819). Each table has state/territory recipient, program, PY2024 amount, PY2025 comparison, and totals. | Final PY2024 totals: **Youth $944,073,800; Adult $883,298,000; Dislocated Worker $1,393,572,000; combined $3,220,943,800**. The Youth/Adult/DW tables provide named state/DC/Puerto Rico rows plus separate outlying-area, Native American, and national-reserve rows. | These are **Program Year 2024 allotments**, not FY2024 payments: PY2024 runs on the WIOA program-year cycle and includes funds available for later obligation/expenditure. DOL says WIOA spending summaries are cumulative accrued expenditures and that states have three years to obligate and expend funds. Keep as program-allocation/award data, not federal outlays. |

## Official portals found but not usable as a complete FY2024 itemized denominator

| Portal | What it offers | Failure or scope result |
|---|---|---|
| **CDC Grant Funding Profiles** | [CDC description](https://www.cdc.gov/funding-profiles/about/index.html); [portal](https://fundingprofiles.cdc.gov/). The portal exposes CSV, XML, and Excel downloads and recipient, geography, category, funding opportunity, and obligation fields. | The public portal currently renders **FY2023** as its latest general profile in the accessible view. FY2024-specific program pages such as PHIG exist and were retained above, but a complete FY2024 CDC-wide CSV/XLS export and exact total were not validated. CDC also excludes contracts, personnel, direct assistance, international activity, and other categories, so the profile is not total CDC spending. |
| **HHS Payment Management System (PMS)** | [HHS Payment Management](https://www.hhs.gov/about/agencies/asa/psc/accounting/payment-management/index.html); [PMS recipient portal](https://pms.psc.gov/grant-recipients/welcome.html). PMS manages drawdowns, disbursements, cash management, and Federal Financial Reports. | No public national FY2024 recipient/payment CSV, JSON, or API was found. PMS requires recipient access, and its cash-drawdown/FFR data is not the same as TAGGS award actions or USAspending obligations. Record as a payment-system lead, not a public validated source. |
| **HUD/CPD — IDIS and consolidated-planning data** | [CPD public system](https://cpd.hud.gov/cpd-public/consolidated-plans); [IDIS extract layouts](https://files.hudexchange.info/resources/documents/IDIS-Online-Appendix-D-Data-Extract-File-Layouts.pdf); [HUD CPD overview](https://www.hud.gov/hud-partners/community). | IDIS layouts describe grant, subfund, activity, grantee, funding source, draw, and expenditure fields, but the public national FY2024 extract requires authorized IDIS access. No public national FY2024 CSV/JSON/XLS with a complete official total was validated. Existing research already records this route as blocked; no duplicate claim is made here. |
| **HUD FY2024 CPD formula allocations** | [HUD CPD program overview](https://www.hud.gov/hud-partners/community); [HUD consolidated-planning framework](https://www.hud.gov/hud-partners/community-conplan). Programs include CDBG, HOME, ESG, HOPWA, HTF, and related CPD formula grants. | HUD's current indexed formula-allocation page exposes later-year workbooks, but a recoverable national FY2024 workbook and exact national total were not validated during this pass. HUD's [FY2024 AFR](https://archives.hud.gov/reports/afr/afr2024.pdf) provides non-federal-physical-property investment aggregates (for example, CDBG $1.295B, CDBG-DR $1.288B, HOME $28M, CoC-Homeless $1M, ESG $0, HTF $1M), but no recipient-level rows; these aggregates are not a CPD award or outlay denominator. |
| **DOL Unemployment Insurance** | [ETA UI data portal](https://oui.doleta.gov/unemploy/DataDashboard.asp?stream=business). It provides state-benefit downloads, annual program/financial data, and claims/benefit measures. | The portal reports **CY2024** regular-program benefits paid of approximately **$34.4B** and 5.3M beneficiaries. It is not FY2024, primarily reflects state UI trust-fund benefits rather than a federal Treasury outlay, and the accessible pass did not validate a complete FY2024 state-by-recipient download. Keep as a related beneficiary-payment lead only. |

## Accounting and inclusion rules for downstream use

1. Do not add TAGGS, NIH, CDC, HUD, or WIOA amounts to the Treasury FY2024 outlay total. They are program-specific award, obligation, allocation, or benefit measures.
2. Prefer the official grand total in each source over recomputing from nested subtotals. For HUD CoC and Capital Fund, the published totals reconcile to the report rows. For CDC PHIG Component B and DOL WIOA, the published recipient/program rows reconcile to the stated program totals.
3. Treat HHS TAGGS's Issue Date FY and Funding FY as separate filters. A FY2024 issue-date result is not automatically a FY2024 funding-year result.
4. Treat CDC's FY2024 PHIG table as a point-in-time grant award snapshot and DOL WIOA as PY2024 availability/allotment data. Neither represents cash drawdowns or Treasury outlays.
5. The research pass itself did not edit JavaScript; the exact compatible slices selected for the explorer are imported in `data/federal/`, while the larger unvalidated portals remain catalogued only.

# FY2024 Federal Expansion: USDA RD, FTA, DOE, NASA, NSF, and NOAA

Research completed 2026-08-19. This is an official-source inventory for possible FY2024 recipient/beneficiary-level spending layers. It supplements, and does not duplicate, the sources already listed in `SOURCE_RESEARCH_ALL_SOURCES.md`.

The exact compatible slices selected from this pass are imported in `data/federal/`: DOL WIOA Youth (**58 rows / $944,073,800**), Adult (**57 rows / $883,298,000**), and Dislocated Worker (**58 rows / $1,393,572,000**) recipient allotments; USDA Rural Development Farm Labor Housing loans (**9 rows / $6,704,105**), Farm Labor Housing grants (**9 rows / $11,441,998**); and NOAA Fisheries Saltonstall-Kennedy recommendations (**16 rows / $6,450,223.39**). They remain separate award/allotment/commitment measures and are not added to the Treasury outlay denominator.

## Reading rules

- `validated` means the official page exposes itemized rows and an official total, and the visible rows were summed or the official count was checked.
- `partial` means an official source exposes useful rows or an aggregate, but not enough accessible data to validate both a national FY2024 row count and total.
- `failed` means the official path was identified but the FY2024 extract could not be retrieved or parsed.
- Award, obligation, loan commitment, recommendation, allocation, and Treasury outlay are different measures. They must remain separate in downstream data.
- No source below should be added to Treasury MTS outlays unless it explicitly reports Treasury outlays. Most sources below report awards or obligations.

## Summary ledger

| Agency | Official source and format | FY2024 itemization | Official count / total | Measure and status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| USDA Rural Development | [Rural Investments Dashboard](https://www.rd.usda.gov/rural-data-gateway/rural-investments/data), CSV export from dashboard | Project/program, geography, fiscal year, investment type; includes recipient/borrower fields where disclosure permits | National FY2024 count/total not validated; dashboard says latest 10 fiscal years | Obligated investment dollars; `partial` because export is JavaScript-driven and no public file URL was exposed |
| USDA Rural Development | [FY24 Farm Labor Housing awards](https://www.rd.usda.gov/media/file/download/usda-rd-fy24-farm-labor-housing-10152024.pdf), PDF | 9 projects, recipients, loan and grant amounts | Loans $6,704,105; grants $11,441,998; total $18,146,103 | Program award commitments; `validated` for this program announcement, not national RD spending |
| FTA | [FY24 Bus and Low-No awards](https://www.transit.dot.gov/funding/grants/fy24-fta-bus-and-low-and-no-emission-grant-awards), HTML table | Project sponsor, state, project description, Bus/Low-No category, funding | Official total $1,497,553,559; page itemizes projects, but row count was not independently machine-validated | Competitive grant awards; `partial` count, validated official total |
| FTA | [DOT FY2024 Annual Performance Report](https://www.transportation.gov/media/276), PDF/HTML report | Aggregate FTA grant/cooperative-agreement count | 2,248 grants and cooperative agreements; more than $21.6B | Awards, not outlays; `partial`, no row-level export |
| DOE | [DOE FY2024 Agency Financial Report](https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2024-12/fy-2024-doe-agency-financial-report_0.pdf), PDF | Program-level IIJA resource/obligation/outlay table; no individual recipients | IIJA net obligations $9.077B; net outlays $1.377B | Agency/program aggregate; `partial`, not a recipient ledger |
| DOE | [PAMS](https://www.energy.gov/science/portfolio-analysis-and-management-system-pams), web search interface | DOE Office of Science financial-assistance awards searchable by institution, PI, and program | FY2024 national count/total not exposed | Grants/cooperative agreements; `failed` bulk-download/total validation |
| NASA | [Procurement Data View](https://prod.nais.nasa.gov/cgibin/npdv/adhoc.cgi), web query interface | Contracts, grants, cooperative agreements, Space Act agreements, and purchase orders; contractor and FY obligations fields | FY2024 national count/total not retrieved | Award obligations, not payments; `failed` query/export validation because the interface requires JavaScript |
| NASA | [FY2024 SBIR/STTR Phase I announcement](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-selects-2024-small-business-research-teams-for-tech-development/), HTML plus linked awardee list | Small-business and STTR awardees; official count and program total | Nearly 250 teams; 209 SBIR businesses and 39 STTR businesses; $44.85M | Selected award funding; `partial` because the linked awardee file was not parsed into a local row count |
| NSF | [Award Search API](https://resources.research.gov/common/webapi/awardapisearch-v1.htm), JSON/XML API | Awardee, program, agency, date, obligated funds, estimated total, award ID | Live schema verified; FY2024 filtered count/total not validated | Award obligations; `partial/failed` FY2024 query validation |
| NSF | [FY2024 Federal S&E Support Survey](https://ncses.nsf.gov/surveys/federal-support-survey/2024), XLSX tables | Agency, institution, state, field, and FY2024 obligations to higher education/nonprofits | Higher-education federal S&E obligations $46.854B; NSF share $6.918B | Survey obligations, not all NSF awards or outlays; `partial` because XLSX rows were not parsed |

| NOAA Fisheries | [Saltonstall-Kennedy 2024 recommended projects](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/national/funding-financial-services/recommended-saltonstall-kennedy-grant-projects), HTML table | 16 projects with applicant, project title, and federal funding amount | Visible rows sum to $6,450,223.39; page states more than $6M | Recommended grant amounts; `validated` table sum, not final obligation/outlay |
| NOAA Fisheries | [FY2024 Prescott recommended awards](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/marine-mammal-protection/fy-2024-recommended-prescott-grant-awards), HTML table | Applicant/project/federal funding requested | 37 grants; regional totals sum to $4,069,728 | Recommended grant amounts; `validated` regional total, not final obligation/outlay |

## USDA Rural Development

### Rural Investments Dashboard — `partial`

The [Rural Data Gateway](https://www.rd.usda.gov/rural-data-gateway) describes the Rural Investments dashboards as ten years of downloadable investment data with program-area, state, county, and congressional-district views. The [national project-level data page](https://www.rd.usda.gov/rural-data-gateway/rural-investments/data) says users can filter fiscal year, geography, program, date, and investment type and export the result. The [data dictionary](https://www.rd.usda.gov/media/file/download/usda-rd-naics-dashboard-data-dictionary-02262025.pdf) defines fiscal year as the federal fiscal year in which investments were obligated and `Investment Dollars` as total investment dollars obligated in selected fiscal years.

Useful fields include borrower name, program/funding code, state, county, investment type, fiscal year, and investment dollars. The dashboard covers direct loans, guaranteed loans, and grants, which are not interchangeable cash measures. Guaranteed-loan amounts are commitments/investments, not Treasury outlays.

The public page is a JavaScript/embedded dashboard. No stable CSV/JSON URL or national FY2024 row count and total could be extracted during this pass. Keep this as a high-value follow-up source, but do not claim a validated national total until the dashboard export is obtained.

### FY24 Farm Labor Housing award announcement — `validated program slice`

The official [FY2024 Farm Labor Housing announcement](https://www.rd.usda.gov/media/file/download/usda-rd-fy24-farm-labor-housing-10152024.pdf) lists 9 projects and itemizes recipient/project-level loan and grant amounts. The visible award totals are:

- Loans: $6,704,105
- Grants: $11,441,998
- Combined announcement total: $18,146,103

This is a specific program announcement, not a national RD FY2024 ledger. Store loan and grant amounts as separate award/commitment measures.

### Other RD official award slices

The [FY24 Rural Innovation Stronger Economy/RIJA bundle chart](https://www.rd.usda.gov/media/file/download/final-fy24-rija-bundle-4-chart-121024.pdf) lists 209 awards, $6,098,137,231 in loans, and $199,784,971 in grants, for a combined $6,297,922,202. It is an itemized program bundle, not all RD spending. The [Virginia FY2024 annual report](https://www.rd.usda.gov/media/file/download/virginia-rd-2024-annualreport-web.pdf) reports $1.37B obligated in Virginia and includes program-level counts and amounts; it is state-specific, not national.

## Department of Transportation / FTA

### FY24 Bus and Low-No awards — `partial`

The [FTA FY24 Bus and Low- and No-Emission Grant Awards](https://www.transit.dot.gov/funding/grants/fy24-fta-bus-and-low-and-no-emission-grant-awards) page is an official HTML itemization with state, project sponsor, project description, award category, and federal funding. Its official total is **$1,497,553,559**. The page was last updated July 26, 2024.

The source reports competitive grant awards/selected funding. It does not report Treasury payments or outlays. Some rows name a state as sponsor on behalf of a transit provider, so preserve the sponsor and beneficiary/operating agency separately when available. The table’s visible row count was not independently machine-validated because descriptions span multiple rendered lines.

### FTA grant/cooperative agreement aggregate — `partial`

The [DOT FY2024 Annual Performance Report](https://www.transportation.gov/media/276) reports that FTA awarded **2,248 grants and cooperative agreements totaling more than $21.6B**, supporting more than 3,000 public transportation providers. This is a useful official aggregate cross-check, but the report does not provide a downloadable recipient-level FY2024 ledger.

### FTA paths that did not yield the requested layer

The [FTA Statistical Summaries](https://www.transit.dot.gov/funding/grants/statistical-summaries) describe TrAMS data with recipient, program, project-scope, ALI, award, and expenditure detail, but the public yearly summaries available on the page stop before FY2024. The [FY2024 apportionment tables](https://www.transit.dot.gov/funding/apportionments/fiscal-year-2024-apportionment-tables-full-year) have downloadable XLSX files, but they are state/program allocations, not recipient awards or payments. Neither should be used as FY2024 FTA outlays.

## Department of Energy

### DOE FY2024 AFR IIJA table — `partial`

The [DOE FY2024 Agency Financial Report](https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2024-12/fy-2024-doe-agency-financial-report_0.pdf) includes an IIJA resources, obligations, and outlays table by program. ### Office of Science PAMS — `failed bulk extraction`

The [Office of Science awards page](https://www.energy.gov/science/office-science-awards) and [PAMS page](https://www.energy.gov/science/portfolio-analysis-and-management-system-pams) identify a public search interface for current and past Office of Science financial-assistance awards back to 2014, searchable by institution, principal investigator, and program. This is the strongest candidate for NASA-wide FY2024 recipient/award obligations, but the public interface requires JavaScript and did not return a reproducible FY2024 CSV/JSON result or total. ### FY2024 SBIR/STTR Phase I announcement — `partial`

This is a higher-education/nonprofit survey subset, not all NSF awards and not Treasury outlays. The linked XLSX files were discoverable but not parsed in the browser environment, so no recipient row count is asserted here.

### NSF payment distinction

NSF’s [PAPPG financial-requirements guidance](https://www.nsf.gov/policies/pappg/24-1/ch-8-financial-requirements-payments) distinguishes the legal obligation created by award acceptance from later advance or reimbursement payments. ## Department of Commerce / NOAA

### NOAA Weather Program Office FY2024 awards — `validated program slice`

The [NOAA Weather Program Office FY2024 funding announcement](https://wpo.noaa.gov/fy2024-notice-of-funding-awards/) reports **6 new projects**, **8 institutions**, and **$3.74M** in total funding. The page lists six project titles and the participating universities/NOAA laboratories. It does not provide a per-recipient amount column or downloadable CSV. Store the $3.74M as a program-level award total, not a payment total.

### NOAA Fisheries Saltonstall-Kennedy — `validated visible-table sum`

The [2024 Saltonstall-Kennedy recommended-projects table](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/national/funding-financial-services/recommended-saltonstall-kennedy-grant-projects) lists **16** applicants/projects and federal funding amounts. Summing the 16 visible amounts gives **$6,450,223.39**. The page describes these as recommended projects, so the amount is a recommended award amount and not proof of final obligation or outlay.

### NOAA Fisheries Prescott — `validated visible aggregate`

The [FY2024 Prescott recommended-awards page](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/marine-mammal-protection/fy-2024-recommended-prescott-grant-awards) lists **37** recommended grants with applicant/project information. NOAA’s [regional summary](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/feature-story/4-million-awarded-marine-mammal-rescue-efforts-through-prescott-grant-program) reports totals of Alaska $207,206, Greater Atlantic $916,414, Pacific Islands $174,772, Southeast $703,291, West Coast $1,301,179, and National $766,866. These sum to **$4,069,728**. NOAA explicitly cautions that recommendation is not final approval/obligation until the grants officer signs.

### Other NOAA itemized paths and failures

- [Cooperative Research Program selected projects](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/funding-financial-services/cooperative-research-program-crp-selected-projects) and [Species Recovery Grants to States](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/national/endangered-species-conservation/funded-species-recovery-grants-states-proposals) expose official recipient/project/award-number/federal-funding tables. The FY2024 aggregate count and total were not validated from the rendered pages.
- [NOAA SBIR awards](https://techpartnerships.noaa.gov/sbir/awards/) links FY2024 Phase I/II PDF award lists, but an exact FY2024 amount total was not exposed in the accessible page.
- [NOAA Grants Online](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/inport/item/12677) is NOAA’s awards system with recipient and funding fields, but no public national FY2024 CSV/API extract was verified. NOAA’s [financial-assistance monitoring page](https://prod-01-alb-www-noaa.woc.noaa.gov/organization/acquisition-grants/financial-assistance-monitoring) confirms that NOAA awards are administered in Grants Online.
- The [NOAA BIL/IRA Awards Explorer](https://prod-01-alb-www-noaa.woc.noaa.gov/news/bil-ira-awards-explorer-find-investments-making-big-difference-for-us-communities) is a multi-year interactive map, not a FY2024-only file; it was not retrievable during this pass. The [Coral Reef FY2024 grants portfolio](https://coralreef.noaa.gov/funding/funded-projects) is also dynamic and did not expose its FY2024 rows/total.
- The Department of Commerce [Investment Map summary](https://www.commerce.gov/news/blog/2025/01/marking-and-mapping-four-years-investing-america) reports multi-year FY2021–FY2024 obligations and approximate NOAA/Commerce totals, but explicitly describes a provisional, non-audit map. It is not a substitute for an FY2024 itemized ledger.

## Recommended normalized fields

For any later extraction, preserve at least:

`source_id`, `agency`, `bureau`, `fiscal_year`, `recipient`, `beneficiary`, `program`, `award_id`, `project_id`, `instrument_type`, `measure`, `basis`, `amount`, `currency`, `official_total`, `official_row_count`, `status`, and `source_url`.

Use values such as `award`, `obligation`, `loan_commitment`, `recommended_award`, `allocation`, `disbursement`, and `treasury_outlay` for `measure`; use `program_slice`, `agency_total`, `survey_subset`, or `national` for `basis`. This prevents the validated program totals above from being mistaken for agency-wide spending or Treasury outlays.

Research date: **2026-08-19**. Scope: official federal websites, APIs, HTML tables, CSV/XLSX exports, and PDFs only. Existing `SOURCE_RESEARCH_FEDERAL*.md` notes were treated as leads and cross-checked. The research pass itself did not edit code; exact compatible layers were subsequently integrated in `data/federal/`.

Exactness rule used here: an itemized layer is called exact only when visible/downloaded amount rows can be independently summed to the source total. Award, allocation, obligation, and outlay are kept as different measures.

## Results at a glance

| OpenFEMA PA projects initially obligated in FY2024 | 21,177 projects / **$26,079,592,243.04** current `totalObligated` | Current cumulative obligation | Exact current cohort, not an FY2024 obligation-flow total |

## DOJ / Office on Violence Against Women

The official [program-sorted table](https://www.justice.gov/ovw/awards/fy-2024-ovw-grant-awards-program) and [state-sorted table](https://www.justice.gov/ovw/awards/fy-2024-ovw-grant-awards-state) each expose **880 recipient-award rows totaling $684,139,571**. Both views independently reconcile to their published grand total.

- Program schema: organization, city, state, award amount, grouped by program.
- State schema: organization, city, award amount, OVW program.
- Measure: award amount / total awards funded, not payment or outlay.
- Period caveat: the official FY2024 scope contains one **$3,000,000** row labeled `OVW Fiscal Year 2023 National Deaf Services Program Invitation to Apply` / `OVW Deaf Serv FY23`. A strict program-label exclusion produces **879 rows / $681,139,571**, but that is an analyst-defined subset, not the published source total.

Independent check after downloading each HTML page:

```python
import pandas as pd

d = pd.read_html("ovw-fy2024-program.html")[1]
a = d[d["Organization Name"].notna() & d["Award Amount"].astype(str).str.startswith("$")].copy()
a["usd"] = a["Award Amount"].str.replace(r"[$,]", "", regex=True).astype(int)
assert (len(a), a.usd.sum()) == (880, 684_139_571)
```

## DOJ / OJP, BJA, OJJDP, and BJS

### BJA

The official [FY2024 awards-by-state PDF](https://www.ojp.gov/sites/g/files/xyckuh241/files/media/document/2024bjaawardsfinal.pdf) contains **2,549 awards totaling $1,867,250,511**. Its 2,549 row amounts sum exactly to the final grand-total token. The official [funding-opportunity-sorted PDF](https://www.ojp.gov/sites/g/files/xyckuh241/files/media/document/2024bjaawardsnofofinal.pdf) has the identical 2,549-amount multiset and total.

Schema: state, city, program office, award number, grantee, congressional district, solicitation title, award amount. Measure: award amount, not payment/outlay. Seventy cleanly extracted award IDs use 2021–2023 vintages, consistent with continuations or supplements; the export's FY2024 scope must drive inclusion rather than the award-number year.

```python
import re
from pypdf import PdfReader

text = "\n".join(page.extract_text() for page in PdfReader("2024bjaawardsfinal.pdf").pages)
amounts = [int(x.replace(",", "")) for x in re.findall(r"\$([\d,]+)", text)]
assert len(amounts) == 2_550
assert sum(amounts[:-1]) == amounts[-1] == 1_867_250_511
```

### Other OJP

- The official [OJJDP FY2024 awards PDF](https://www.ojp.gov/sites/g/files/xyckuh241/files/media/document/2024ojjdpawardsfinal.pdf) reconciles **419 rows / $476,928,741**. Six rows use `15PBJA-24` IDs for OJP community-violence initiatives, so this is the OJJDP-published/OJP scope rather than a pure `PJDP`-prefix slice.
- The BJS [State Justice Statistics page](https://bjs.ojp.gov/programs/state-justice-statistics-program/state-profiles) and [FY2024 CSV](https://bjs.ojp.gov/sites/bjs/files/media/document/FY%202024%20SJS%20Awards.csv) reconcile **31 recipient rows / $3,915,847**. ## FEMA / DHS

### FY2024 Preparedness Grant Programs

|---|---:|---:|

The component sum is **$1,979,437,779.90**, which rounds to the bulletin's **$1,979,437,780** total. These are final award/allocation measures, not cash outlays. The bulletin explicitly excludes AFG ($291.6 million), SAFER ($324 million), FP&S ($32.4 million), and RCPGP ($10.8 million), which were to be awarded separately.

The separate official [FY2024 EMPG NOFO HTML](https://www.fema.gov/grants/preparedness/emergency-management-performance/fy-24-nofo) independently exposes the same **57 jurisdiction rows / $319,550,000** when the Republic of the Marshall Islands is included. This direct HTML route succeeded even where print/PDF routes returned 403.

The official [updated FY2024 State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program allocations PDF](https://www.fema.gov/sites/default/files/documents/fema_gpd_fy24-slcgp-ib-updated-allocations_01082025.pdf) adds another exact allocation layer: **56 jurisdictions**, with both the original and updated columns independently summing to **$279,873,562**. South Dakota's updated allocation is $0 and its former amount is redistributed, so the updated column should replace rather than be added to the original column.

The preparedness bulletin's State Homeland Security Program and Emergency Management Performance Grant tables are now imported as separate exact layers: **56 rows / $373,500,000** and **56 rows / $319,500,000**, respectively. Both are allocation measures rather than cash outlays. The remaining tables are retained here as source research because their cohort totals and row shapes are mixed (urban areas, grouped nonprofit tables, compact funding, and other recipient classes).

The public [FP&S award search](https://www.fema.gov/es/grants/preparedness/firefighters/safety-awards?page=0) advertises organization, state, program, award amount, award date, and CSV fields, but returned HTTP 403; no FY2024-filtered count or total was validated. ### OpenFEMA Public Assistance cohort

The official [dataset metadata](https://www.fema.gov/api/open/v1/OpenFemaDataSets?$filter=name%20eq%20%27PublicAssistanceFundedProjectsDetails%27), [field metadata](https://www.fema.gov/api/open/v1/OpenFemaDataSetFields?$filter=openFemaDataSet%20eq%20%27PublicAssistanceFundedProjectsDetails%27%20and%20datasetVersion%20eq%202), [project API](https://www.fema.gov/api/open/v2/PublicAssistanceFundedProjectsDetails), and [applicant CSV](https://www.fema.gov/api/open/v1/PublicAssistanceApplicants.csv) are public and require no authentication.

- `totalObligated`: **$26,079,592,243.04**
- `mitigationAmount`: **$1,386,123,451.47**

This is not an FY2024 obligation-flow total. It is a current snapshot of projects **initially** obligated during FY2024: 2,521 rows have a `lastObligationDate` after 2024-09-30, and the API does not expose the transaction history needed to isolate FY2024 changes. FEMA's metadata also says the financial data comes from Grants Manager rather than its official financial system and is not intended for official federal reporting. Preserve the measure as current cumulative obligation and the snapshot date (API `lastDataSetRefresh`: 2026-08-18).

## National Science Foundation

### NCSES institution tables

The official [FY2024 Federal S&E Support Survey](https://ncses.nsf.gov/surveys/federal-support-survey/2024) provides itemized XLSX tables in thousands of dollars.

### Award Search failures

The [Award Search API documentation](https://resources.research.gov/common/webapi/awardapisearch-v1.htm) defines `dateStart`/`dateEnd` by initial award or amendment date, not obligation fiscal year. A FY2024 date query returned `totalCount: 10000`, while display results are capped at 3,000; using it as an obligation-year filter would also omit FY2024 increments on older awards.

The [annual award-download page](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/download-awards) currently says no export files are available. API-document retrieval returned HTTP 403 in one browser path; the official Tableau details view errored, and its CSV probe returned HTTP 200 with a one-byte blank response. No exact NSF-wide FY2024 recipient-obligation export was validated.

## Economic Development Administration

The official [2024 Grant History](https://www.eda.gov/grants/2024) reconciles **362 calendar-year announced investments / $463,036,876**. It is announcement history, not verified obligation dates or outlays.

Wholly contained FY2024 announcement windows total **402 investments / $464,734,859.75**, but the September 26–October 3 batch spans the fiscal-year boundary and contains 19 investments / $60,105,592 without row-level action dates. No exact national FY2024 result can therefore be derived from these pages. The wholly contained [September 19–26 detail page](https://www.eda.gov/grants/september-19-26-2024) is an exact partial slice: **36 recipient/project rows / $97,863,084**.

The [FY2024 Good Jobs Challenge awardee index](https://www.eda.gov/funding/programs/good-jobs-challenge/2024) links eight recipient pages whose `Approximate Award Amount` values sum to **$25,000,000**. The [master announcement](https://www.eda.gov/news/press-release/2025/01/14/us-department-commerce-awards-25-million-latest-installment-good-jobs) is dated 2025-01-14, so this is an FY2024 program/appropriation cohort announced in 2025, not verified FY2024 obligation or outlay activity.

The official [Commerce FY2024 Annual Performance Report](https://www.commerce.gov/sites/default/files/2025-01/FY-2024-APR.pdf) returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare challenge. Indexed text reports only a rounded thematic subset (“nearly $131 million” across 110 manufacturing-related awards) without visible recipient rows; it is not an exact EDA denominator.

## Import recommendation

The exact NOAA Prescott, CRP, BTRP, Species Recovery, BREP, BJS, FEMA SHSP, FEMA EMPG, and FEMA SLCGP rows are now imported in `data/federal/` as separate award/recommendation/allocation layers. Strong remaining candidates are OVW, BJA, OJJDP, and the other FEMA preparedness tables; OpenFEMA is usable only as a dated current-obligation cohort. NOAA Pacific Islands, the two rounded NSF recipient tables, and EDA's period-spanning announcement history must retain their reconciliation/period qualifications and should not be presented as exact FY2024 national spending.

## NSF — Federal S&E Support Survey

NSF’s National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics publishes FY2024 Federal Science and Engineering Support Survey tables. Tables 8–18 provide agency, state, institution, activity, R&D, and recipient-institution views. Table 13 is the most relevant recipient/agency table and is available as an official XLSX and PDF: [Table 13 XLSX](https://ncses.nsf.gov/pubs/nsf26320/assets/data-tables/tables/nsf26320-tab013.xlsx), [Table 13 PDF](https://www.nsf.gov/pubs/nsf26320/assets/data-tables/tables/nsf26320-tab013.pdf), [FY2024 survey landing page](https://ncses.nsf.gov/surveys/federal-support-survey/2024).

The survey measures FY2024 obligations to higher-education and nonprofit recipients, not all NSF awards and not Treasury outlays. The official cross-agency survey total for higher-education S&E obligations is $46.854 billion, of which NSF accounts for $6.918 billion; that is a survey-scope cross-check, not an NSF-wide spending total. The XLSX/PDF table route was identified, but an exact Table 13 row count and independent sum were not completed here, so no row count is asserted.

The NSF Award Search API remains a separate possible award-level route: [official API documentation](https://resources.research.gov/common/webapi/awardapisearch-v1.htm). Its schema exposes awardee, amount obligated, program, agency, date, ID, and total count, but a reproducible FY2024 national filter and total were not validated in this pass. The official annual award-download page currently says downloadable award files are unavailable: [NSF download page](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/download-awards).

DOE’s Research & Innovation Act database describes a searchable listing of unclassified R&D project contracts, grants, cooperative agreements, FFRDC task orders, and other transactions, with original-award fiscal-year data from FY2009 onward and quarterly updates. The database route did not yield a stable downloadable FY2024 CSV/JSON or a validated national count/total in this pass. [Official DOE database description](https://www.energy.gov/cfo/articles/research-innovation-act-database)

The DOE FY2024 Agency Financial Report remains useful for measure separation: the prior research note identified FY2024 Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act net obligations of $9.077 billion and net outlays of $1.377 billion. Those are department/program aggregates without recipient rows, so they should not be joined to award tables as if they were the same measure. [Official DOE FY2024 AFR](https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2024-12/fy-2024-doe-agency-financial-report_0.pdf)

## DOI / National Park Service

The DOJ/OJP NIJ funded-projects search is an all-years catalog and reports 7,496 awards/$3,980,544,205 across all years; it is not a validated FY2024 denominator. The BJA FY2024 awards-by-state PDF exposes recipient and award amount fields, but a national exact row count and total were not completed in this pass. [Official NIJ search](https://nij.ojp.gov/funding/awards/list) and [official BJA FY2024 PDF](https://www.ojp.gov/sites/g/files/xyckuh241/files/media/document/2024bjaawardsfinal.pdf)

## FEMA / DHS — routes that did not validate

FEMA’s Fire Prevention & Safety award-search page exposes Organization, State, Program, Award Amount, Award Date, and a CSV option, and reports 1,108 search results overall. The public route returned HTTP 403 during retrieval, and an FY2024-filtered count/total was not validated. FEMA’s FY2024 Regional Catastrophic Preparedness Grant Program announcement states a $10.8 million FY2024 allocation and promises recipient/award details, but the official PDF route returned HTTP 403, so no exact rows were extracted. [Official FEMA RCPGP announcement](https://www.fema.gov/sites/default/files/documents/fema_gpd-fy24-rcpgp-award-announcement-ib.pdf)

FEMA’s FY2024 Preparedness Grant Programs information bulletin reports $1,979,464,968 across the preparedness programs, but the accessible document did not produce a complete recipient-level export. This aggregate cannot substitute for row-level awards. [Official FEMA bulletin](https://www.fema.gov/sites/default/files/documents/fema_gpd-fy24-preparedness-grants-ib.pdf)

FEMA GO requires an authenticated recipient workflow, and the Public Assistance summary is an interactive view over the OpenFEMA Public Assistance Funded Projects Details API. Neither route yielded a validated FY2024 national recipient/project count and total in this pass. [FEMA GO](https://www.fema.gov/grants/guidance-tools/fema-go/startup) and [Public Assistance summary](https://www.fema.gov/data-visualization/public-assistance-program-summary-obligations)

## Commerce / Economic Development Administration

Commerce’s FY2024 Annual Performance Report search result states that EDA invested nearly $131 million across 110 awards in FY2024. The official PDF route was blocked during retrieval, so recipient rows and an exact unrounded total were not extracted. [Official Commerce FY2024 APR](https://www.commerce.gov/sites/default/files/2025-01/FY-2024-APR.pdf)

EDA’s FY2024 Good Jobs Challenge page names eight FY2024 awardees, but does not provide exact per-recipient amounts on the accessible page. [Official EDA FY2024 awardees](https://www.eda.gov/funding/programs/good-jobs-challenge/2024)

EDA’s “2024 grant history” page is a calendar-year 2024 weekly investment history, not a federal fiscal-year FY2024 table. Summing the listed calendar-year entries produces 362 investments/$463,036,876, but this result is intentionally not used as FY2024 spending because the source’s time basis is calendar year. [Official EDA 2024 grant history](https://www.eda.gov/grants/2024)

## Other failed or semantically unsuitable routes

- USDA Rural Development: the prior expansion note documented official FY2024 award/program pages and the RD public data/API limitations. No additional complete FY2024 recipient-level CSV/JSON/XLSX with an exact official total was validated in this continuation. Keep RD award data separate from Treasury outlays.
- NASA NPDV: the official contractor/payment data interface is query/JavaScript dependent; a reproducible FY2024 export and national exact total were not obtained. [Official NASA NPDV help](https://prod.nais.nasa.gov/cgibin/npdv/npdvhelp.cgi)
- NOAA Climate Resilience Regional Challenge: NOAA reports almost $573 million and describes 22 coastal-zone projects plus 8 research-reserve projects, but the companion downloadable award PDF returned 404, preventing a complete exact row/total cross-check. [Official project page](https://www.coast.noaa.gov/funding/resilience-challenge/projects.html)
- NOAA Ocean Exploration FY2024: NOAA reports four projects and more than $2.1 million, but the page does not provide a complete exact total or all four project-level amounts. [Official NOAA page](https://oceanexplorer.noaa.gov/news/fy24-funding-awards/)
- NOAA Marine Debris: NOAA’s official search result reports 13 FY2024 projects and more than $23 million, but the award page returned 403 and the exact itemized total was not extracted. [Official NOAA page](https://marinedebris.noaa.gov/funding-opportunities/noaa-marine-debris-program-awards-13-new-projects-funding-remove-marine-debris-under-bipartisan-infrastructure-law)
- NSF annual award download: the official page currently reports that downloadable award files are unavailable, so the API remains schema-validated but not nationally reconciled for FY2024. [Official NSF page](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/download-awards)
- EDA FY2024 APR: official source exists, but PDF retrieval was blocked; do not infer exact totals from the rounded “nearly $131 million” search-result wording.

## Import and reconciliation guidance

1. The FTA AIM table, HUD PRICE/Section 811/Jobs Plus/Community Compass/ICDBG tables, and the visible OIA project table are the strongest new row-level additions. Preserve the program name, fiscal year, recipient, amount, and `basis=award`.
2. Do not combine award totals with Treasury outlays. DOE’s FY2024 AFR illustrates the distinction: obligations and outlays differ materially even within one program family.
3. Treat NOAA Pacific Islands’ 14-organization/$7,023,719 figure, NASA’s 15-project/$15.6 million figure, DOI/NPS’s 54-project/$254.68 million figure, and the DOE $473.6 million formula-grant figure as program aggregates unless a complete itemized export is separately captured. OIA’s eight visible rows are imported only as a partial visible slice.
4. Treat rounded language (“nearly,” “more than,” “almost,” or “approximately”) as non-exact. Record the exact count where the source provides one, but do not invent an exact dollar total.
5. No commits were made. The six HUD/FTA tables and the partial OIA table are imported separately from the Treasury denominator.

## Integration status

The seven imported award tables from this report are now in `data/federal/`: FTA AIM, HUD PRICE, HUD Section 811, HUD Jobs Plus, HUD Community Compass, HUD ICDBG, and the partial OIA visible-award slice. They remain separate award measures outside the Treasury outlay denominator. EPA, NOAA Pacific Islands, NASA, DOI/NPS, DOE, NSF, DOJ, FEMA, and EDA remain catalogued-only where the report did not provide a complete exact recipient-amount layer.

Research-only inventory; checked 2026-08-18. No spending amounts are asserted or imported here. Every link below is an official state agency, legislature, comptroller, auditor, treasurer, or state open-data source.

## Reusable import shape

Prefer a source-specific raw snapshot, then normalize each record to:

```json
{
  "state": "XX",
  "fiscal_year": 2025,
  "source_id": "state-portal-or-dataset-id",
  "source_url": "https://official.example.gov/…",
  "source_type": "payment|payroll|grant|contract|budget|acfr",
  "basis": "cash|budgetary|accrual|unknown",
  "payment_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "recipient": "vendor/person/program recipient",
  "agency": "paying agency",
  "department": "department or cabinet",
  "program": "program/account/function",
  "fund": "fund or funding source",
  "object": "expense/object class",
  "amount_usd": 0,
  "record_id": "source transaction or award id",
  "status": "reported|redacted|excluded",
  "notes": "source caveat"
}
```

Use `amount_type` (`payment`, `outlay`, `obligation`, `budget`, or `award`) when the source exposes it. Do not add records across different bases or fiscal periods. Keep `source_url`, source record identifiers, exclusions, and raw snapshots so totals can be reproduced.

Highest-priority adapters are direct CSV/XLSX/API/OData exports; second priority is an interactive portal with an official download; ACFRs and budget books are reconciliation sources, not substitutes for transaction rows. Connecticut publishes payee, department, program, account, fund, payment ID, and amount fields in its state open-expenditure dataset; Maryland publishes an OData payment dataset; New Jersey publishes downloadable agency, authority, and combined expenditure datasets; Nevada publishes a bulk CSV expense download; North Dakota publishes biennium Excel downloads; Texas publishes downloadable state expenditure data; and California documents raw-data downloads for Open FI$Cal. ([CT](https://data.ct.gov/Government/State-of-CT-Open-Expenditures-Ledger-Current/ajdm-rvz7), [MD](https://opendata.maryland.gov/Budget/State-of-Maryland-Payments-Data-FY2008-to-FY2024/7syw-q4cy), [NJ](https://www.nj.gov/transparency/financial-management/expenditures/index.shtml), [NV](https://open.nv.gov/), [ND](https://www.omb.nd.gov/financial-transparency/dashboards/mass-download), [TX](https://comptroller.texas.gov/transparency/reports/expenditures-by-county/), [CA](https://fiscal.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/Transparency-Site-Fact-Sheet_12.23.24FVADA.pdf))

- Structured retry queue: [data/source-failures.json](data/source-failures.json) records every deferred, access-blocked, wrong-period, scope-limited, or corrupted route without treating it as validated spending.
- Schema check: the proposed fields are the intersection of fields explicitly exposed by official sources, with nullable fields for states that only publish aggregates or PDFs. CT, Delaware, NJ, Nevada, North Dakota, Texas, and California are the best first adapters because their official pages document field-level exports or downloads.
- Basis check: do not reconcile checkbook cash/payment rows directly to ACFR accrual totals. Texas explicitly warns that its payment database and ACFR differ in accounting treatment; Rhode Island labels its portal raw cash data; Maine labels checkbook data unaudited; Washington lists excluded payment systems. ([TX](https://fmx.cpa.texas.gov/fmx/systems/ose/faq.php), [RI](https://www.ri.gov/opengovernment/disclaimer), [ME](https://opencheckbook.maine.gov/helpfaqs.html), [WA](https://www.fiscal.wa.gov/Spending/DisclaimerWAVendorCB.pdf))
- Access failures recorded as skipped/deferred—not corrupted data: New Hampshire's expenditure-register ZIP was only partially transferred; Idaho still lacks a reproducible public FY2024 bulk result; Hawaii and South Dakota expose wrong-period or aggregate-only alternatives. Arizona's official General Fund hierarchy and West Virginia's two published vendor rankings are imported independently of their blocked bulk routes.
