- Kansas's [KanView data-download center](https://kanview.ks.gov/DataDownload.aspx) yielded all four official FY2024 quarterly vendor-payment CSVs. The checked-in [data/state-ks/state-ks.js](data/state-ks/state-ks.js) contains 1,063,608 source rows, 121,797 agency/business-unit + vendor + account + fund groups, and an exact `$31261239621.45` total. KanView labels 39 Q1 records with July 2024 payment dates as FY2024; those records are retained under the portal's fiscal-year semantics.
- South Dakota's [FY2024 ACFR](https://bfm.sd.gov/ACFR/SD_ACFR_2024.PDF) activity rows reconcile exactly to $6,315,971,000 in [the jurisdiction hierarchy](data/department-index.js). [Open SD](https://open.sd.gov/) did not expose a validated FY2024 transaction export.
- South Carolina's [Comptroller monthly spending file listing](https://cg.sc.gov/fiscal-transparency/monthly-state-spending-transparency-files) yielded all 12 official FY2024 CSVs. The checked-in [data/state-sc/state-sc.js](data/state-sc/state-sc.js) contains 1,893,314 central-accounting source rows, 131,763 agency/vendor/category/fund groups, and an exact `$36704047552.46` total. This is explicitly partial: the Comptroller excludes the Public Service Authority, Education Lottery Commission, Jobs-Economic Development Authority, and state-supported colleges/universities.
- Tennessee's current [Transparent Tennessee checkbook](https://www.tn.gov/transparenttn/finances/checkbook.html) links an official [Tableau CSV](https://data.tn.gov/t/Public/views/SearchableCheckbookPublic_17861130451500/Agency.csv?:showVizHome=no). FY2024 branch controls total `$33097780967.41` exactly; a separate public agency export contributes 10 non-additive rows totaling `$2468346318.02`, while protected payments remain summarized. These controls are imported in [data/state-tn/state-tn.js](data/state-tn/state-tn.js). The official [FY2024 ACFR](https://www.tn.gov/content/dam/tn/finance/acfr/ACFR_FY24.pdf) is additionally imported as 12 non-additive primary-government function rows totaling `$47759686000`.
- Louisiana's official [vendor-payment search](https://checkbook.la.gov/vendorSearch.cfm) accepted FY2024 and reported 29,851 vendor aggregate records with payee and total-payment fields; the official [expenditure search](https://checkbook.la.gov/expenditures2.cfm) exposes fiscal year, department, agency, category, and expense-type filters. The public surface remains interactive and paginated, with no validated statewide bulk export or transaction-level download for the full FY2024 result set; the reconciled department aggregate is imported in [data/state-la/state-la.js](data/state-la/state-la.js).
- Louisiana's official [department JSON](https://checkbook.la.gov/cfcChartDataExpenditures.cfc?method=funct_getUpdatedDepartmentTotals&fiscalyear=2024&returnformat=json) contains 28 FY2024 department rows totaling `$43394706192.68`; the independent [expense-category JSON](https://checkbook.la.gov/cfcChartDataExpenditures.cfc?method=funct_getUpdatedStateObjectCatTotals&fiscalyear=2024&returnformat=json) sums to the same amount. These controls are imported in [data/state-la/state-la.js](data/state-la/state-la.js); the 29,851-record vendor search remains interactive and is not treated as a validated bulk itemized export.

### Washington FY2024 checkbook detail import (2026-08-19)

- The official [FY2024 workbook](https://fiscal.wa.gov/Spending/VendorPayments2325.xlsx), sheet `FY 2024`, contains 496,769 rows and sums to `$34,960,860,261.78`. Grouping by agency, object, category, subobject, and subcategory produces 3,202 rows across 101 agencies with an exact cent match.
- Each detail file under [data/state-wa](data/state-wa) keeps the receiving agency, accounting-program label, aggregate amount, and source-row count. Vendor names are not stored, including where the workbook contains personal payee names; salary-related rows remain organization/accounting-class aggregates.
- The layer is intentionally not scaled to the Census statewide ledger: the workbook excludes salaries, debt, refunds, higher education, lottery prizes, client services, and other systems listed in the official [disclaimer](https://www.fiscal.wa.gov/Spending/DisclaimerWAVendorCB.pdf). The Census comparison difference remains metadata in [data/state-wa/state-wa.js](data/state-wa/state-wa.js); no unsupported residual row is added.

### Texas FY2024 cash-report hierarchy (2026-08-25)

- The official [FY2024 cash-report data ZIP](https://comptroller.texas.gov/transparency/reports/cash-report/2024/data/data.zip) supplies 2,032 Net Expenditures groups and 1,146 Other Uses groups. One Other Uses group combines two identical source schedule rows, so the 3,178 stored groups preserve 3,179 source-row counts.
- Grouping both sections by their source-native agency labels produces 158 agency controls totaling `$377841427258.09`. Every agency card now links back to its fund and expenditure/use rows under [data/state-tx/archive-state-source](data/state-tx/archive-state-source), with exact parent and statewide reconciliation.
- The cash-report Table 1 control remains `$2293940.84` higher than the imported schedules, as already documented. No synthetic variance or recipient/vendor names were added; the detail layer remains a cash-report fund/use hierarchy.

## Import-time validation

For each source snapshot:

1. Preserve the raw file/response and retrieval timestamp.
2. Validate required fields: source URL, fiscal period, amount, and at least one of recipient, agency, program, or account.
3. Normalize currency to USD without rounding away source precision; record whether the row is payment, outlay, obligation, award, budget, or accrual.
4. Deduplicate only on a source-provided transaction/record ID; otherwise retain rows and flag possible duplicates.
5. Sum normalized rows by the source's own fiscal period and compare with the source's published total. Keep exclusions and redactions as metadata rather than silently treating them as zero.
6. Cross-check the resulting period total against the state's ACFR/budgetary report only after documenting basis, scope, branch coverage, and off-system exclusions.

- Alaska blocker: the official [Checkbook Alaska](https://checkbook.alaska.gov/) ledger API `https://stateofalaska.data.socrata.com/resource/qdjq-crxc.json?$select=fy%2Ccount%28%2A%29%20as%20rows&$group=fy&$order=fy%20desc&$limit=100` returned only `FY 2026: 17,764 rows`; the FY2024 aggregate query against the same official ledger returned `source_rows=0`, with no FY2024 expenditure/payment rows. The dataset schema has department, expense category/type, vendor name, and amount fields, but FY2024 is unavailable in the public machine-readable ledger, so no `data/state-ak/state-ak.js` was created.

### Virginia FY2024 expenditure import (2026-08-18)

- The official [FY2024 expenditure ZIP](https://www.datapoint.apa.virginia.gov/data/extracts/2024/All%20Expenditures%20for%20Fiscal%20Year%202024.zip) contains 12 monthly CSVs with the same 14-column schema and FY2024 dates from `2023-07-01` through `2024-06-30`.
- Validation completed: `sourceRows=3140325`, the source-level `AGENCY_NAME + VENDOR_NAME + CATEGORY_NAME` grouping has `104115` rows, and both source and vendor/category grouped totals equal `$83966509424.97` with `$0.00` delta.
- The checked-in explorer layer [data/state-va/state-va.js](data/state-va/state-va.js) uses a compact `AGENCY_NAME + PROGRAM_NAME + CATEGORY_NAME` grouping with `5069` rows; its total also equals `$83966509424.97`. Negative adjustments and blank vendor values were retained in source validation metadata.

### Florida FY2024 vendor-payment import (2026-08-18)

- The official [Florida DFS Vendor Payments page](https://myfloridacfo.com/transparency/vendorpayments) identifies FY2024 as a downloadable full-fiscal-year ZIP of pipe-delimited text files and states that Florida’s fiscal year runs July 1–June 30. The linked official file is [fy2024-vendor-payments.zip](https://myfloridacfo.com/docs-sf/default-source/transparency-docs/vendor-payments/fy2024-vendor-payments.zip?sfvrsn=6b8f34a8_1).
- The official response returned HTTP 200, `Content-Type: application/x-zip-compressed`, and `Content-Length: 110405839`. The archive was reconstructed from explicit byte ranges and passed `unzip -t` integrity validation.
- The layout document defines 20 pipe-delimited fields, including agency code/name, vendor number/name, object code/name, and signed amount. The four FY2024 files contain 3,300,414 valid rows totaling `$128747111750.18`.
- The checked-in [data/state-fl/state-fl.js](data/state-fl/state-fl.js) uses a compact 2,786-row agency/object grouping that equals the validated source total. The official ZIP remains linked for vendor-level quarterly detail.

- Illinois vendor boundary: the official [Comptroller payments page](https://illinoiscomptroller.gov/financial-reports-data/find-a-report/payments) supports named-vendor searches for the last three fiscal years; it is not a statewide FY2024 vendor export. The agency layer is therefore intentionally labeled partial rather than recipient-level complete.

- Indiana FY2024 import: the official [Indiana Data Hub Vendors Data package](https://hub.mph.in.gov/api/3/action/package_show?id=ae7baff7-69ec-410e-8554-7b5dbb712aa7) exposes four machine-readable CSV resources with Agency Name, Vendor Name, Expenditure Category, Amount, Fiscal Year, and source identifiers: [Q1](https://hub.mph.in.gov/dataset/ae7baff7-69ec-410e-8554-7b5dbb712aa7/resource/fc01be5a-af0c-4d68-a7df-42be69b231c4/download/vendor_2024q1.csv), [Q2](https://hub.mph.in.gov/dataset/ae7baff7-69ec-410e-8554-7b5dbb712aa7/resource/e8f1f264-887a-4407-8618-56a0d99108d4/download/vendor_2024q2.csv), [Q3](https://hub.mph.in.gov/dataset/ae7baff7-69ec-410e-8554-7b5dbb712aa7/resource/a2ae5342-af84-446f-bff9-a1bdcc99d1c0/download/vendor_2024q3.csv), and [Q4](https://hub.mph.in.gov/dataset/ae7baff7-69ec-410e-8554-7b5dbb712aa7/resource/bde8c376-5554-4ebc-ba3a-397521c22448/download/vendor_2024q4.csv). Combined source count is `1,217,545` and total is `$8,063,068,063.680`. The checked-in [data/state-in/state-in.js](data/state-in/state-in.js) uses a compact 678-row agency/category grouping that equals the official total; the linked quarterly CSVs retain vendor-level detail.

### California FY2024 partial vendor import (2026-08-18)

- The official [Open FI$Cal download index](https://open.fiscal.ca.gov/download-expenditures.html) exposes twelve FY2024 monthly vendor files through the official [pointer CSV](https://adwoutputfilesadlsstore.blob.core.windows.net/transparency/MonthlyVendorTransactionPointer/MonthlyVendorTransactionPointer.csv). The files include business unit, agency, department, document, accounting date/period, vendor, account category, fund/program, and monetary amount fields; FY2024 periods cover July 2023 through June 2024.
- The official [vendor-vs-spending scope documentation](https://open.fiscal.ca.gov/learning-center/spending-vs-vendor-reports.html) states that vendor files omit payroll, social-service bulk payments, EFTs, purchase-card transactions, expedited payments, and non-FI$Cal departments. The portal currently covers about 79% of budgetary expenditures, and its [FAQ](https://open.fiscal.ca.gov/faq.html) warns that raw files are unaudited and do not reconcile to statewide financial statements.
- All twelve FY2024 files were downloaded and validated: 3,586,591 source rows totaling `$76144875021.960`; every row has `fiscal_year_begin=2024` and its expected accounting period. Grouping by agency, department, vendor, and account category/description produces 110,830 rows with the same subtotal. The checked-in [data/state-ca/state-ca.js](data/state-ca/state-ca.js) links all twelve official files and remains explicitly partial because the vendor layer omits payroll, bulk social-service payments, EFTs, purchase-card transactions, expedited payments, and non-FI$Cal departments.
- This vendor subtotal is not added to the Census pie denominator; the pie continues to use the reconciled statewide Census finance layer while the California click-through exposes the validated vendor subset.

### Kentucky FY2024 spending hierarchy (2026-08-25)

- The official [Kentucky Transparency Spending Search](https://transparency.ky.gov/search/Pages/spendingsearch.aspx) loads its FY2024 controls from the published [spending hierarchy API](https://secure2.kentucky.gov/TransparencyWebApi/v1/SpendingAndVendorDetail?dataGroupingView=BranchView&requestYear=2024&maxReturnRows=1&startingIndex=0). The Branch view returns Executive and Judicial controls; Executive drills through 12 cabinets to 163 departments, while Judicial drills directly to 27 expense classes.
- The 190 aggregate detail rows reconcile to every cabinet or branch to the cent and therefore to the official statewide total of `$49421121460.56`. They are stored under [data/state-ky/archive-state-source](data/state-ky/archive-state-source) without retaining vendor names.
- The API separately reports 381,730 vendor records and limits the detailed response/export to 10,000 rows. Vendor-level statewide coverage therefore remains deferred; the checked-in archive claims only the complete cabinet/branch hierarchy verified above.

### North Carolina FY2024 actual-budget import (2026-08-18)

- The official [NC Open Budget page](https://www.nc.gov/government/open-budget) documents FY2024 bulk budget data and identifies the state accounting source, agency/payee/category concepts, and CSV downloads. Its vendor-payment section lists only [FY2024 Q1](https://www.nc.gov/nc-vendor-payment-data-fy-2024-q1/download?attachment=), followed by FY2023 and earlier full-year files; no FY2024 Q2–Q4 or full-year vendor-payment export is listed.
- The official FY2024 budget CSV contains 205,602 rows: 68,534 each for Actual, Budget, and Adjusted Budget. The Actual `Requirement` rows total `$73513647447.20`; receipts plus appropriations equals Requirement with zero row-level equation failures.
- The checked-in [data/state-nc/state-nc.js](data/state-nc/state-nc.js) uses a compact 424-row agency/category grouping that equals the official Actual total. The separate vendor-payment listing remains Q1-only, so this layer is labeled actual budget requirements rather than vendor payments.

### Michigan FY2024 checkbook import (2026-08-19)

- The official [Open Michigan bulk checkbook export](https://sigmai.michigan.gov/EI360TransparencyApp/jsp/bulkCheckbookDownload) contains 688,287 FY2024 rows with department, object category/group, vendor, check date, and check amount fields. Exact displayed-row cents and independent quarter totals sum to `$72708027060.60`; the official footer count matches and footer total is `$72708027060.59`, a preserved $0.01 source variance. The checked-in [data/state-mi/state-mi.js](data/state-mi/state-mi.js) groups the rows into 346 department/object-category/object-group records without changing any amount. Michigan excludes private/confidential/protected, payroll, pension, public-assistance, medical, and tax-refund payments.

### Vermont FY2024 vendor-payment import (2026-08-18)

- The official [SFY 2024 Vendor Payments view](https://data.vermont.gov/Finance/SFY-2024-Vendor-Payments/5t78-kzns) exposes `qtrending`, agency, vendor, description/category, account/object, fund, and amount fields. Its API returned 150,438 rows totaling `$7445364768.85`.
- Quarterly controls returned 34,821 / `$2194418362.24`, 37,119 / `$1916454446.29`, 37,934 / `$1445153228.60`, and 40,564 / `$1889338731.72`; both counts and amounts sum exactly to the statewide view. See [data/state-vt/state-vt.js](data/state-vt/state-vt.js).

### Wyoming FY2024 itemized import (2026-08-25)

- The official [WyOpen FY2024 page](https://www.wyopen.gov/main/year/2024) links to the [transaction search](https://www.wyopen.gov/search) and [Download Results](https://www.wyopen.gov/search/csv) endpoint. Twelve bounded monthly exports from July 2023 through June 2024 reproduce all **1,245,917** annual query results without the one-shot export's truncation.
- The hierarchy groups **1,100,556 classified positive line items** to **107 agencies** and **5,268 expenditure-category/description rows**, totaling **$6,548,654,149.67** exactly. The remaining **16,009 blank-category positive rows / $1,088,608,655.37** and **129,352 non-positive rows / -$8,910,389,410.99** remain explicit reconciliation controls rather than being force-netted into spending.
- WyOpen's exclusions and WOLFS payment basis make this a partial itemized scope, not an ACFR-equivalent statewide denominator. The official [FY2024 State Auditor ACFR](https://sao.wyo.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/2024-ACFR-State-of-Wyoming.pdf) function/activity layer totals **$5,402,901,937** and remains linked as non-additive context.

### Mississippi FY2024 aggregate import (2026-08-19)

- The official [Mississippi DFA Transparency page](https://www.dfa.ms.gov/transparency) links the [Transparency Mississippi expenditure reports](https://www.transparency.ms.gov/expenditures/stateExpendituresByAgencyNamePrint.aspx) and identifies an “Expenditures by Vendor” report. The official [Expenditures by Vendor FAQ](https://www.dfa.ms.gov/sites/default/files/inline-files/expenditures-by-vendor-faqs-1.pdf) describes interactive vendor-specific queries requiring the first three characters of a vendor name and lists warrant/expense-type information, but does not provide a statewide FY2024 CSV/JSON download.
- The official [Statewide Expenditures Download](https://boe.magic.ms.gov/Transparency/AVXFJs06_thHjAH84iLYV7g) still redirects to credentialed SAP UI5logon (`PBA`, client `100`). The official [FY2024 ACFR](https://www.dfa.ms.gov/sites/default/files/Financial%20Reporting%20Home/Publications/ACFR/FY24%20%20ACFR%20Final.pdf) reports $22,863,250,000 of governmental activity expense and $1,055,187,000 of business-type activity expense. The two rows reconcile exactly to $23,918,437,000 in [the jurisdiction hierarchy](data/department-index.js); no transaction-level amounts were fabricated.
- The official state-expenditure endpoint returned only an HTML report shell (`State Expenditures`) without a machine-readable export. The checked-in layer is therefore explicitly ACFR aggregate-only rather than a receiver/vendor export.

### Louisiana FY2024 agency drill-down (2026-08-25)

- The official [Louisiana Checkbook expenditure page](https://checkbook.la.gov/expenditures2.cfm) publishes 28 FY2024 department controls totaling `$43394706192.68`; the independent [expense-category JSON](https://checkbook.la.gov/cfcChartDataExpenditures.cfc?method=funct_getUpdatedStateObjectCatTotals&fiscalyear=2024&returnformat=json) sums to the same statewide amount but remains a separate dimension.
- With the public session set to FY2024, the official [department drill-down route](https://checkbook.la.gov/filteredResults2.cfm) returned agency totals for every department. The resulting 153 agency rows reconcile to each department to the cent and therefore to the statewide control. They are stored under [data/state-la/archive-state-source](data/state-la/archive-state-source) and linked from the Louisiana archive summary.
- Vendor detail remains interactive and no statewide machine-readable vendor export was validated. The archive therefore claims department-to-agency coverage only; it does not treat the separate expense-category feed as a department crosswalk or fabricate recipient rows.

### Indiana FY2024 packaging note (2026-08-18)

- The four official Indiana Data Hub CSVs were downloaded and validated: Q1 317,044 rows / $2,265,155,707.790; Q2 302,650 rows / $2,041,843,199.080; Q3 303,810 rows / $1,713,044,831.530; Q4 294,041 rows / $2,043,024,325.280. All rows had FY2024, required agency/vendor/category/amount fields, and `PeopleSoft Financials` as the source; the combined validated count was 1,217,545 and total $8,063,068,063.680.
- An earlier packaging attempt stopped after grouping validation; this was superseded by the checked-in compact 678-row [data/state-in/state-in.js](data/state-in/state-in.js), which reconciles to the same official source count and total.

### Montana FY2024 aggregate import (2026-08-19)

- The official [Montana Transparency portal](https://transparency.mt.gov/) identifies [Checkbook Accounts Payable](https://tableau-ext.mt.gov/t/DOA/views/SABHRSCheckbookAccountsPayable/AccountsPayableDashboard) as the statewide payment source. FY2024 can be selected, but the dashboard states that the `Agency` filter is required before searching; with no agency selected it displays no data.
- The official [FY2024 ACFR](https://montanaveba.mt.gov/_docs/sfsd/sab/Montana-ACFR-2024-sig-on-file.pdf) reports $8,355,107,000 of governmental activity expense and $613,160,000 of business-type activity expense. The two rows reconcile exactly to $8,968,267,000 in [the jurisdiction hierarchy](data/department-index.js). The checkbook remains agency-filtered, so no transaction-level Montana rows were imported.

### Nebraska FY2024 checkbook import (2026-08-18)

- The official [Nebraska State Spending FY2023-24 checkbook](https://statespending.nebraska.gov/FiscalYearExpenditures) reports 1,039,429 records totaling `$8,824,754,417.13` when fiscal-year value `2024` is selected. The export schema is `id`, payment date, payee, amount, payer, comment, budget, purchase order, and agency name.
- Twelve bounded official CSV postbacks (July 2023 through June 2024) were downloaded and reconciled: 1,039,429 rows and `$8,824,754,417.13`, exactly matching the portal controls. After removing person-level Net Pay and employee-reimbursement names, grouping by agency, payee, payer, comment, budget, and purchase order produces 143,112 privacy-safe explorer rows in [data/state-ne/state-ne.js](data/state-ne/state-ne.js); sensitive rows are organization-aggregated with counts only.
- The portal documents exclusions for aid/retirement payments and protected functions. The checked-in layer therefore claims the portal’s statewide checkbook scope, not every state-finance flow outside that portal.

### Nevada FY2024 OpenBudget import (2026-08-18)

- The official [Nevada FY2024 expenditure summary](https://openbudget.nv.gov/OpenGov/ViewActualSummary.aep?fiscalYear=2024&filter=null&view=ObjectSeries) links the [bulk actual-expenditure CSV](https://openbudget.nv.gov/OpenGov/DownloadExpenditures.aep?mode=Actual&fiscalYear=2024&format=csv). Its fields are function, department, division, budget account, category, general ledger, vendor, and amount.
- The downloaded export contains 88,953 rows totaling `$23,980,496,026.03`; grouping by department, division, budget account, category, general-ledger description, and vendor produces 88,807 rows with the same total in [data/state-nv/state-nv.js](data/state-nv/state-nv.js).
- Receiver coverage is partial by source design: 18,990 rows have blank vendor fields and total `$12,053,606,575.60`. Those records remain in the layer under `[no vendor in source]`; the official department/category totals are still complete for this export.

# FY2024 state transaction-portal follow-up audit

Research date: **2026-08-19**. Scope: official checkbook, vendor-payment, agency, category, accounting-system, and open-data routes for **Arizona, Idaho, Mississippi, Montana, New Hampshire, South Dakota, Utah, Alaska, Colorado, Wyoming, and West Virginia**.

This report records the source findings. West Virginia's 300 published vendor ranks were subsequently promoted as a bounded hierarchy; its 22-cabinet layer remains linked context and the complete raw vendor export remains unavailable.

## Method and acceptance rules

- FY2024 means July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024 unless the state source defines a different period.
- I inspected the state agency/treasurer/controller/auditor route, its documented export or API surface, and a separate official FY2024 financial-report control.
- A transaction layer is accepted only when the period is proven, the returned/displayed rows can be counted and summed, and the source's own total or an independent same-scope control can be reproduced.
- A difference of **less than $1.00** is an agreement. A difference of $1.00 or more is retained as a discrepancy.
- ACFR/comparative statements are reconciliation controls, not substitutes for receiver-level transactions. “0 accepted” means no reproducible FY2024 transaction layer was accepted; it does not mean zero spending.
- “Observed” figures below are portal observations from this audit. They are not claimed to be statewide denominators when the source excludes, masks, caps, or aggregates populations.

## Executive result

| State | Best official FY2024 result | Disposition |
|---|---:|---|
| Arizona | **913 FY2024 General Fund program rows / 66 agencies / $37,497,268,015** | Published budgetary actuals reconcile exactly; General Fund scope only. |
| Idaho | 0 accepted transaction rows; FY2024 control **2 / $15,073,867,000** | Vendor-detail reports are documented but requestable/authenticated rather than public bulk downloads. |
| Mississippi | 0 accepted transaction rows; FY2024 control **2 / $23,918,437,000** | Vendor/agency/category fields are documented; the statewide report did not yield a reproducible FY2024 export. |
| Montana | 0 accepted transaction rows; FY2024 control **2 / $8,968,267,000** | Official AP and credit-card Tableau routes returned an unexpected error during export inspection. |
| New Hampshire | 0 accepted transaction rows; FY2024 comparative control **12 / $10,029,340,000** | Official FY2024 expenditure-register ZIP returned 403. |
| South Dakota | **248,350 / $4,302,394,530.14**, but dates are FY2025 | Prior-year CSV is exact for its own period, not FY2024; FY2024 transaction total remains unvalidated. |
| Utah | **100 accepted FY2024 ranked vendors / $38,356,170,590.45** | State of Utah top-100 result reproduced; 99 named rows plus one blank rank-1 row. Bounded ranking, not an all-vendor denominator. |
| Alaska | **17,764 / $484,447,249.65**, but the public ledger is FY2026 | Checkbook is current-fiscal-year only; FY2024 transaction rows were unavailable. |
| Colorado | **1,033,925 FY2024 transactions / 24 departments / 2,577 expense-code rows / $39,210,596,217.87** | Twelve bounded TOPS month exports reconcile exactly; transfers and adjustments remain excluded by source policy. |
| Wyoming | **1,245,917 query rows**; **1,100,556 classified positive rows / 107 agencies / 5,268 category-description groups / $6,548,654,149.67** | Twelve bounded exports reconcile exactly; exclusions and separate adjustment controls prevent use as a complete statewide denominator. |
| West Virginia | **300 vendor ranks / $3,915,581,065**; cabinet context **22 / $20,428,646,141**; full query **3,502,057 / $19,005,950,270.47** | Each layer reconciles internally and remains separately scoped. |

## State-by-state findings

### Arizona

**Official routes inspected:** [OpenBooks Expenditures](https://openbooks.az.gov/expenditures), its download rules, and the official [FY2024 State financial report](https://www.azauditor.gov/sites/default/files/2026-04/StateOfArizonaJune30_2024FinancialReport_1.pdf).

OpenBooks remains inaccessible through the challenged bulk route, and its filtered current-view export is capped at 50,000 lines. The financial report provides a reproducible alternative rather than a receiver list: pages 179–196 publish General Fund budgetary actuals by agency and program.

The extracted schedule contains **913 program rows across 66 agencies / $37,497,268,015**, exactly matching the printed total. Controls retain **838 positive rows, 74 zero rows, and one negative adjustment**. It is explicitly a General Fund budgetary scope, not all funds or government-wide expenses.

The same report's prior government-wide function/activity layer has **12 rows / $62,548,895,000** and remains linked as non-additive context.

**Disposition:** resolved partial hierarchy. Promote the exact agency/program schedule; keep OpenBooks and the ACFR layer as separate, differently scoped sources.

### Idaho

**0 public FY2024 rows accepted, total not established.** No fabricated row count was substituted for the requestable report. The [FY2024 ACFR](https://transparencyresources.idaho.gov/CAFRDocuments/2024%20Annual%20Comprehensive%20Financial%20Report.pdf) control is governmental activities **$12,850,063,000** plus business-type activities **$2,223,804,000** = **$15,073,867,000**, an exact two-row agreement.

**Official routes inspected:** [DFA Transparency Mississippi](https://www.dfa.ms.gov/transparency), the [state expenditure report](https://www.transparency.ms.gov/expenditures/stateExpendituresByAgencyNamePrint.aspx), the official [data dictionary](https://www.transparency.ms.gov/files/DataDictionary.pdf), [MAGIC Finance and Grants Management](https://www.dfa.ms.gov/magic-finance-and-grants-management), and the [FY2024 appropriation bulletin](https://www.dfa.ms.gov/sites/default/files/Budget%20and%20Fund%20Home/Annual%20State%20Appropriation%20Budget%20Bulletins/FY2024%20Appropriations%20Budget%20Bulletin.pdf).

The official data dictionary is unusually useful for a future normalized layer. It defines agency, vendor, transaction, expended amount, expense code, expense type, accounting year/month, and fiscal coding. Its expense types include personal-services salaries, travel, contractual services, commodities, capital outlay, subsidies, loans, and grants. The DFA transparency hub also links contract/grant interfaces and expenditure-by-vendor reports.

The report surface reached a credentialed or non-exportable state during this pass; no statewide FY2024 row file could be reproduced and cross-summed. **0 rows accepted, total not established.** The FY2024 appropriation bulletin is a budget/authority source, not proof of cash spent, so it is not used as a transaction substitute.

The official [FY2024 ACFR](https://www.dfa.ms.gov/sites/default/files/Financial%20Reporting%20Home/Publications/ACFR/FY24%20%20ACFR%20Final.pdf) control is governmental activities **$22,863,250,000** plus business-type activities **$1,055,187,000** = **$23,918,437,000**, exact across its two activity rows.

**Official routes inspected:** [Montana Transparency](https://transparency.mt.gov/), the [Montana Data Portal finance dataset listing](https://data.mt.gov/Datasets?search=2024), [SABHRS Accounts Payable](https://tableau-ext.mt.gov/t/DOA/views/SABHRSCheckbookAccountsPayable/AccountsPayableDashboard), [SABHRS Credit Card Payments](https://tableau-ext.mt.gov/t/DOA/views/SABHRSCheckbookCreditCardPayments/CreditCardPaymentDashboard), and [Montana ACFRs](https://montanaveba.mt.gov/SFSD/ACFR-PAFR).

The data portal lists the AP and credit-card datasets, but the linked Tableau views returned **“Unexpected Error”** before a reproducible agency-filtered export could be obtained. **0 FY2024 statewide AP rows accepted, total not established.** No partial agency result was promoted to statewide data.

The official [FY2024 ACFR](https://montanaveba.mt.gov/_docs/sfsd/sab/Montana-ACFR-2024-sig-on-file.pdf) control is governmental activities **$8,355,107,000** plus business-type activities **$613,160,000** = **$8,968,267,000**, exact across the two activity rows.

**Official routes inspected:** [TransparentNH](https://www.transparentnh.das.nh.gov/), the [TransparentNH glossary](https://www.transparentnh.das.nh.gov/resources/glossary), the official [FY2024 expenditure-register ZIP](https://www.transparentnh.das.nh.gov/sites/g/files/ehbemt1071/files/documents/expenditure-register-2024.zip), [Governor's expenditure reports](https://www.transparentnh.das.nh.gov/where-money-goes/governors-expenditure-reports), and the [FY2025 Single Audit containing FY2024 comparative expenses](https://www.gc.nh.gov/lba/Budget/FiscalItems/2026-04-17_Agenda_Items/Single_Audit_2025.pdf).

### South Dakota

**Official routes inspected:** [BFM financial-transparency hub](https://bfm.sd.gov/), [prior-year checkbook detail CSV](https://bfm.sd.gov/ledger/CheckbookDetailPriorYear2.csv), [Vendor Self Service](https://bfm.sd.gov/vendor/), and the [FY2024 ACFR](https://bfm.sd.gov/ACFR/SD_ACFR_2024.PDF).

The official BFM hub links checkbook, contracts, grants, payroll, and vendor services. Vendor Self Service requires a TIN and either a payment/invoice identifier or a vendor PIN, so it is not a public statewide bulk export.

The public prior-year CSV yielded **248,350 rows / $4,302,394,530.14**. Date inspection showed **2024-07-01 through 2025-06-27**, which is FY2025 under South Dakota's July–June calendar. **Official routes inspected:** [Transparent Utah Vendor Payments Search](https://transparent.utah.gov/entities/vendor-payments-search), [Highest Paid Vendors](https://transparent.utah.gov/entities/highest-paid-vendors), its official query backend, the legacy search documentation, and the stale [Utah Open Data expenditure mirror](https://opendata.utah.gov/Government-and-Taxes/State-of-Utah-Expenditures-Transparency-/dqdf-hweu).

The Division of Finance says Checkbook Alaska is updated monthly and reports expenditures, revenues, and fund balances for the **current fiscal year**. The public ledger schema exposes fiscal year, department/division, vendor, expense category/type, fund, payment status, dates, and amount.

The official ledger aggregation returned **FY2026: 17,764 rows / $484,447,249.65**. A FY2024 filter returned no expenditure/payment rows. This is a wrong-period/current-year result, not a FY2024 import. The FY2024 travel workbook is a travel-office cost/savings analysis, not a statewide spending ledger. The FY2024 SWCAP is also not a FY2024 transaction ledger: the official page says that report is based on actual expenditures from FY2022.

The [FY2024 ACFR](https://doa.alaska.gov/dof/reports/resource/2024acfr.pdf) control is governmental activities **$11,372,389,000** plus business-type activities **$360,641,000** = **$11,733,030,000**, exact across its two activity rows.

**Disposition:** current-year API/wrong period. Keep the schema and query endpoint; re-run when the public ledger exposes FY2024 rows or a historical download.

### Colorado

**Official routes inspected:** [TOPS Expenses](https://data.colorado.gov/stories/s/TOPS-Expenses/pqw4-6m8r/), the [TOPS overview](https://data.colorado.gov/stories/s/Transparency-Online-Project-TOPS-State-Government-/fjyf-bdat/), the [TOPS CSV view](https://tableau.state.co.us/t/DPA_TOPS/views/TOPSExpenses/TOPSExpenses.csv?:showVizHome=no), and the [FY2024 ACFR](https://content.leg.colorado.gov/sites/default/files/fy2024_acfr_final.pdf).

**Official routes inspected:** [WyOpen FY2024 dashboard](https://www.wyopen.gov/main/year/2024), [WyOpen transaction search](https://www.wyopen.gov/search), [limitations/completeness page](https://www.wyopen.gov/main/readmore), the official [search CSV route](https://www.wyopen.gov/search/csv), and the [FY2024 ACFR](https://sao.wyo.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/2024-ACFR-State-of-Wyoming.pdf).

It remains non-additive accounting context because the WOLFS checkbook has a different payment scope.

**Disposition:** accepted as a reproducible, exact itemized partial hierarchy. Do not treat it as a complete statewide or ACFR-equivalent denominator.

### West Virginia

**Official routes inspected:** the State Auditor's [FY2024 vendor page](https://stories.opengov.com/westvirginia/published/1Y5McMyl2), filtered OpenGov view, [FY2024 State Dollar Report](https://www.wvlegislature.gov/legisdocs/reports/agency/A06_FY_2024_26612.pdf), and FY2024 ACFR.

The State Dollar Report publishes two bounded tables. The top-200 non-purchasing-card list sums to **$3,792,384,742**; the top-100 purchasing-card list sums to **$123,196,323**. The tables do not claim all-vendor coverage. Six vendor labels repeat across ranks/channels and are kept distinct. The report's explanatory text has one FY2023/FY2024 wording conflict, but its table titles, report period, and rank sequences identify the FY2024 tables; this caveat is retained.

The same report's **22 cabinet rows / $20,428,646,141** remain a separate cash context layer. Its object-class display is $2 below that cabinet total, so the object table is not promoted. The filtered OpenGov view reports **3,502,057 rows / $19,005,950,270.47**, but the raw file remains unavailable.

| South Dakota | $6,141,833,000 + $174,138,000 = $6,315,971,000 | Exact. |
| Utah | Top-100 vendors $38,356,170,590.45; ACFR context $22,117,390,000 | Each layer reconciles internally; scopes are non-additive. |

| Wyoming | $5,014,428,038 + $388,473,899 = $5,402,901,937 | Exact. |

## Failure and follow-up ledger

- **Blocked or non-exportable:** New Hampshire FY2024 register ZIP partial transfer; Idaho requestable/authenticated reports; West Virginia full vendor export generation. West Virginia's bounded 300-row rankings are imported independently.
- **Wrong period:** Alaska public Checkbook is FY2026 and South Dakota prior-year CSV is FY2025. Colorado's prior current-period probe was superseded by the reproduced FY2024 TOPS hierarchy.
- **Capped/stale:** Arizona OpenBooks filtered exports are capped at 50,000 lines, but the financial-report hierarchy is imported separately; Utah's old mirror stops in 2018, but its current FY2024 top-100 ranking is imported separately.
- **Incomplete by design:** Arizona is General Fund budgetary scope; Utah is top-100 vendors; West Virginia is two bounded vendor rankings with protected/full-query populations outside the slice; Wyoming and Colorado have stated exclusions. None is presented as a complete statewide denominator.
- **Internal source discrepancy:** West Virginia's displayed object-class rows are $2 below the published total. This exceeds the project's less-than-$1 agreement rule, so only the cabinet table is accepted as an exact layer.
- **Scope disagreement:** West Virginia's ranking, cabinet cash, full-query, and ACFR totals are separate measures. Wyoming's top-10 controls likewise are not combined into a statewide denominator.

## Reproduction notes

The report preserves official URLs, periods, row counts, totals, exclusions, and cross-check decisions. Re-running the audit should first attempt the blocked full-year files, then validate every returned period field before summing; no commit was made.
